Why We Love It
Soaps can strip your skin of moisture, so they aren’t usually recommended for dry skin, but you still need something to cleanse your body when bathing.
CeraVe Hydrating Body Wash
contains three types of ceramides to protect and restore your skin’s moisture barrier while soothing itchiness. It’s made specifically for itchy, sensitive skin and is free from harsh chemicals like parabens and sulfates, so it’s safe for you and your growing baby. This body wash is thick, so some people do note that it can be tough to squeeze out of the bottle and recommend storing it upside down to make the creamy wash flow out more easily.
Leah Rocketto, What to Expect’s Associate Commerce Director, didn’t find this to be a major deterrent. “Because it was thick, I was able to use less of it which was not only cost-effective, but better for my skin.” Leah switched to CeraVe early in her pregnancy and noticed relief within a few weeks. She also noticed an improvement in her
keratosis pilaris
, a condition that causes patches of tiny bumps to form on the skin. “Within a few months of using CeraVe’s body wash, I noticed my skin was smoother,” Leah says. “The bumps didn’t disappear completely, but that small reduction made me feel a little more confident, which isn’t always easy to feel during pregnancy.”
Sarah Darby, What to Expect’s Senior SEO Content Strategist, swears by CeraVe products for dry skin, both while pregnant and not pregnant, because the ingredients are gentle on her skin. “I also would use CeraVe on my belly in pregnancy,” she says. “While it didn't prevent stretch marks because I am super prone to them, it definitely provided relief from itching.”
Moms who love this body wash say it’s great for layering and follow up with CeraVe moisturizer post-shower, which contains many of the same soothing ingredients. Use this gentle cleanser if you want to kick-start your moisturizing routine and ease itchiness.

Why We Love It
When topical treatments only go so far to soothe itchy pregnancy skin, a cool mist humidifier can work wonders to keep skin hydrated as they “keep the air from being too dry in your home,” Dr. Han explains. Not only will it boost your skin’s moisture level as you sleep, but it’ll come in handy later on if your baby has a stuffy nose, dry skin, or eczema. The
Crane Ultrasonic Cool-Mist Drop Shape Humidifier
is easy to fill and clean, so it’s perfect for having on hand when you need to add extra moisture to the air.
I have had a Crane humidifier like this one for nearly a decade, and it’s still going strong through two kids and many, many late nights with congestion. It’s a bit bulky though, so you may have to clear off some space on your nightstand if you want to keep it right next to you while you sleep. If you’re looking for a more long-term option to avoid dry skin and keep itchiness at bay, moms in our community agree that a humidifier is worth the investment, as you’ll likely use it for years to come with your little one.
What to Look For In Itchy Skin Remedies
When shopping for products that can relieve itchy skin during pregnancy, consider the following:
Ingredients:
Look for products with gentle, soothing ingredients like oats or other natural moisturizers, including shea butter, coconut oil, avocado oil or aloe. The ingredient list should be simple and easy to understand — simple products are often better for maintaining the skin barrier, says Dr. Han. Pick pH-balanced products that contain ceramides, which are
lipids that restore the skin’s barrier
, and are free from harsh chemicals like sulfates and parabens to best help retain moisture and not cause further aggravation.
Fragrance-free:
Added fragrances can further irritate itchy pregnancy skin, so it's best to skip products with scents listed in the ingredient list. When it comes to picking products for itch relief, Dr. Han says, "the less fragrance, the better." Choose products labeled "fragrance-free" or "no added fragrance." Additionally,
pregnancy can heighten the senses
, and added fragrances could trigger an unpleasant reaction like nausea. You may also want to avoid essential oils, too, which can sometimes function as fragrances and irritate or cause allergic reactions.
Frequency of application:
Keeping the skin moisturized is priority number one when dealing with itchy skin, whether you’re pregnant or not. It's important to note that this process
may require applying various products
in layers to tame the flame. From the soap or body wash you use while showering to the lotions, creams and oils you apply after bathing, each product can add another layer of moisturizing protection to soothe skin. You may need more than one application per day or need to experiment with different layering techniques until you find what works best for your itchy skin. Most of the products on this list can be used in tandem with each other, so you might want to try a few out, especially if you’re dealing with severe dry skin. And, keep in mind that the best time to apply moisturizer is right after taking a shower or bath when your skin is damp.
FAQ
What causes itchy skin during pregnancy?
Dry skin during pregnancy
is one of the most common causes of itchiness, and can happen anywhere on the body. Additionally, changes in hormone levels, your immune system and the environment can sap the skin of its natural oils, leading to dryness. When your skin's natural barrier is compromised, nerve endings in the top of the skin become irritated and sensitive. Some beauty products and even clothing can make this worse.
As your pregnancy progresses,
your belly may also start to itch
because your expanding baby bump stretches your skin, which stretches nerve endings and triggering itchiness.
There are some conditions related to itchy skin during pregnancy that you might want to keep an eye on, as they might require additional treatment. For instance, an itchy belly accompanied by a rash may be
pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy (PUPPP)
or polymorphic eruption of pregnancy (PEP). These annoying but benign conditions appear in some expecting moms (usually starting around the third trimester, but sometimes sooner), are possibly linked to genetic causes, and disappear after childbirth.
Any skin conditions you have that would cause itchy skin before becoming pregnant may also flare up as your immune system responds to pregnancy and your hormones shift. "If you have eczema, sometimes it can worsen during pregnancy as well," Dr. Han says. Though your doctor is your best resource for treating medical skin conditions during pregnancy, over-the-counter products can temporarily relieve itching.
How can you treat itchy skin during pregnancy?
Many simple solutions can effectively soothe itchy skin during pregnancy at home. "The first thing we try to address are simple issues such as increasing your moisturizer use and gentle bathing techniques," Dr. Han says. Bathing with a gentle cleanser and applying a lotion daily often does the trick to keep skin moisturized and supple. If you find that your usual products aren’t doing the trick, you may need to switch things up to find what works best to soothe your itchy skin. Make sure your products are following the guidelines we set out earlier — such as being fragrance-free and contain soothing ingredients.
Keep showers or baths short (
five to 10 minutes, per AAD guidance
), and avoid using hot water. "I usually recommend using warm instead of hot water,” says Dr. Han. “The fats in your skin that serve to keep in the moisture have relatively low melting points. Once you step out of the shower, evaporative cooling can actually draw even more moisture from your skin." After bathing, gently pat the skin with a soft towel, and apply any moisturizers directly on damp skin.
You can layer heavier pH-balanced creams with naturally moisturizing ingredients and ceramides to lock in moisture and protect the skin's natural barrier. Talk to your doctor about using an anti-itch lotion with natural ingredients like calamine or menthol, which can produce a cooling effect to ease itchiness. For an
itchy belly during pregnancy
, a belly balm or vitamin E oil will also help moisturize your skin.
Other strategies you can try include using a humidifier in your bedroom at night to keep the air moist, which helps moisturize the skin. Wearing loose-fitting clothing can also alleviate pressure or reduce friction against your skin, which can intensify the irritation and lead to worsening itch. Many expecting moms also use ice packs or cool strips of cloth draped over the skin to temporarily relieve itchy pregnancy skin.
Never hesitate to contact your practitioner, too, if the itch persists, you notice a rash or you're otherwise concerned. "We should be able to help with this, so don't suffer through scratching your skin up and not getting enough rest," Dr. Han recommends.

You just got that big fat positive and you’re going to be a parent. Congratulations!
The first trimester of pregnancy is an exciting — albeit often uncomfortable — time. Your
breasts may be tender
, you might
feel more tired than usual
and you may experience some
morning sickness
. While it’s all considered typical of pregnancy, it’s not always fun.
With that, it’s only natural to search for things to help your body better adjust to growing a baby. Luckily, there are tools out there that can help.
Of course, it’s easier said than done knowing exactly which products might help you feel better — they don’t teach this kind of thing in school, and you don’t automatically know how to deal with all the
changes that can come in the first trimester
. Here’s what you need to know.
What kinds of products do you need during the first trimester?
The first trimester has a reputation for being a little rough, and with good reason — your body is going through a lot of changes, says Christine Greves, M.D., an OB/GYN at the Winnie Palmer Hospital for Women and Babies in Orlando, Florida. “Some women may feel tired, a little nauseous and even have vomiting,” she says. “But it all depends.”
Food aversions can lead to changes in your diet, which may make you feel a little off, too, she says. And, of course, you’re growing a new life inside you — that takes a lot of energy.
When it comes to the first trimester, there are a few essential items that many moms-to-be find especially helpful during those first weeks. These products
help alleviate nausea
caused by morning sickness, ensure that you and baby are getting all the vitamins and nutrients you need and keep your changing body as comfortable and content as possible. Just keep this advice in mind, per Dr. Greves: “Do what feels right for you. You’re in survival mode at this time.”
How we chose the best first trimester pregnancy must-haves
We started by scouting out the most popular first trimester products on the market, including What to Expect readers’ favorites and what doctors have seen their pregnant patients find success with. Then, we narrowed down our picks to the top-reviewed and best-rated items to select products that are designed to help you get through this period of pregnancy with relative ease.
Check out our first trimester shopping checklist below for all the must-haves you'll want on hand those first few months.

Hydration is crucial
during your pregnancy. “Your blood volume is expanding so you need the liquid for that,” Greves says. And, she points out, if you’re struggling with morning sickness, you need to replace fluids you’re losing. “Hydration can just help you feel better overall,” she adds. Make sure you always have cold H2O ready to go with this
Yeti Rambler
. It has a double-walled vacuum to keep your drinks cold (or hot) for hours and holds up to 18 ounces at a time (a great size for day-to-day use). A wide bottle mouth makes it easier to drink lots of liquids at once, while sturdy construction means it can stand up to accidental drops. And, of course, you can use this well beyond pregnancy.

On the laundry list of not-so-lovely pregnancy symptoms,
constipation
is most certainly up there. Not only is it a hallmark of early pregnancy, but for some women it lingers throughout the entire 9 months and into the postpartum period.
Like most pesky pregnancy side effects, hormones are usually to blame, namely progesterone. In an effort to prevent premature labor, progesterone quiets muscular contraction in the uterus, as well as other organs, including the gut and colon, explains Felice Gersh, M.D., an OB/GYN in Irvine, California. Add to that the fact that your growing baby is taking up more and more space in your uterus, plus any changes in your diet as a result of pregnancy cravings or aversions, and you have a recipe for constipation.
For some unlucky women, constipation can start as soon as they begin taking their prenatal vitamins and continue throughout pregnancy, notes Sherry Ross, M.D., OB/GYN and Women’s Health Expert at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, California.
How To Help Relieve Pregnancy Constipation
Eat the rainbow.
When you’re pregnant, it’s more important than ever to
eat a healthy diet
with plenty of leafy greens, crunchy peppers, super squash, antioxidant-packed fruits and berries, chia seeds (try soaking them in milk overnight) and whole grains. Not only do these foods benefit your little one's development, they’re packed with fiber to help your digestion humming right along. Another fiber-packed ingredient?
Makeover meal time.
Aim to eat five small meals a day rather than three big ones. Not only will this give your system time to catch up, it also keeps you from getting hangry.
Flat or sparkling?
Keep pouring and drinking water — 12 to 13 glasses a day will help keep your digestive track lubricated and make your poop softer (which makes it easier to go). Decaffeinated tea (iced or hot), hot water with lemon, and fruit and veggie-infused waters are other
hydrating choices
.
Keep moving.
When you want things to get moving, you gotta get moving. Even a 10-minute daily walk can be enough to boost circulation to keep you regular.
Don’t hold back.
To prevent constipation, it’s important to go when you feel the urge.
Talk to your doctor.
Many prenatal supplements include iron, which, while beneficial for you and your baby, can cause constipation. If you suspect this might be the case, ask your doctor if she can recommend an alternative supplement.
If you’re experiencing pregnancy constipation, hang in there! Constipation usually eases up after your baby is born. In the meantime, here are some products that might help relieve your symptoms.

Your first trimester symptoms have come and gone — good riddance, morning sickness! — but once you’re in your second or third trimester, there are new pregnancy symptoms on the horizon like
ankle and foot swelling
and even
congestion
. Another unfortunate symptom that might appear around the second trimester?
Pregnancy hemorrhoids
.
Hemorrhoids are varicose veins in or around the rectum that can be itchy and painful, especially while sitting or pooping. During pregnancy, these swollen, twisted veins are
usually caused by poor blood flow
and increased pressure within your lower pelvis, says
Aimee Eyvazzadeh, M.D.
, a board-certified OB-GYN. And it’s no surprise that you might experience
postpartum hemorrhoids
, too.
“This pressure could be due to the growing fetus, pushing during labor or differences in bowel movements [during pregnancy],” Dr. Eyvazzadeh says. “Increased progesterone levels can cause slowing of the gut and less frequent bowel movements or constipation, which could cause more hemorrhoids.”
Thankfully, we’re here to help with advice and vetted over-the-counter hemorrhoid medications to help relieve discomfort and pain. And, if you’re also experiencing postpartum hemorrhoids from delivery, don’t worry — you can certainly use these products after baby is born, too.
How We Chose the Best Products for Pregnancy Hemorrhoids
We spoke with Dr. Eyvazzadeh to learn what causes hemorrhoids during pregnancy and what hemorrhoid relief products are safe to use while pregnant.
We utilized feedback from pregnant and formerly pregnant people in the What to Expect Community to find a variety of products that provided hemorrhoid relief. We included products that received numerous positive reviews and were deemed:
Easy and comfortable to use
Provides fast relief
How Do You Treat Hemorrhoids During Pregnancy?
Modifying your diet and habits
can significantly reduce hemorrhoids
during and after pregnancy. But for hemorrhoids you experience during pregnancy, Dr. Eyvazzadeh says you may want to consider the following:
Try to have regular bowel movements that are not too hard; taking stool softeners could help
Drink a lot of non-caffeinated fluids
Get regular exercise, especially cardio activities like walking or swimming, which can increase blood flow and help prevent hemorrhoids
Take measures
to prevent constipation
, like eating a high-fiber diet
Avoid sitting for long stretches of time by moving around to take the pressure off the veins in your pelvic area
Using witch hazel pads can help
relieve pain and reduce swelling
Soak in a warm bath
Do Pregnancy Hemorrhoids Go Away?
Typically, yes, hemorrhoids during pregnancy tend to go away after delivery. But don’t think that it’s as instant as “baby out, hemorrhoids gone,” because hemorrhoids
can still happen within
one month postpartum.
“Medication commonly given during labor can cause constipation and hemorrhoids,” says Dr. Eyvazzadeh. She advises patients to start taking a stool softener a few weeks prior to their due date to try and avoid constipation and unnecessary straining before delivery, but you’ll want to ask your doctor if that’s right for you.
Although hemorrhoids aren’t typically a cause for concern,
hemorrhoids that worsen
despite lifestyle changes and over-the-counter treatments may mean it’s time to talk to your doctor. Possible surgical treatment after pregnancy may be discussed. And if you
notice any bleeding
, speak with your doctor. Even though it could be a normal symptom of hemorrhoids or an anal fissure, it’s better to be on the safe side.

The hormonal ups and downs of pregnancy can be unpredictable and lead to a host of unanticipated side effects, with
acne
being one of them. However, the causes of these breakouts differ from those in non-pregnant individuals. Not to mention many skincare ingredients need to be avoided during pregnancy, so finding a pregnancy-safe acne treatment that effectively clears your skin is essential.
According to Kate Viola, M.D., a board-certified dermatologist at
Dermatology Partners
, the various changes that occur during pregnancy — such as increased blood flow, oil production, and fluctuating hormones — can lead to acne. "Physiological changes [during pregnancy] include increased skin sensitivity, pigmentation, superficial vessels, and dryness, as well as worsening of pre-existing skin conditions," she explains. Women undergoing hormonal fertility treatments, like
in vitro fertilization
(IVF) or
intrauterine insemination
(IUI), may also experience heightened skin sensitivity, which can contribute to acne.
However, as mentioned earlier, your usual acne treatment might not be safe during this time. While you should ultimately consult with your dermatologist and OB/GYN to find a pregnancy-safe acne treatment, we’ve compiled a list of such treatments to help get you started.
How We Chose the Best Pregnancy-Safe Acne Treatments
To compile our list of the best available pregnancy-safe acne treatments, we first consulted four dermatologists:
Anne Truitt
, M.D., a board-certified dermatologist in San Diego, California;
Kate Viola
, M.D., a board-certified dermatologist at Dermatology Partners in Sparks, Maryland;
Stephanie Saxton-Daniels
, M.D., a board-certified dermatologist at Westlake Dermatology in Dallas, Texas; and Gary Goldfaden, M.D., a board-certified dermatologist and founder of
Goldfaden MD
. We spoke to them, and referenced recommendations from the
American Academy of Dermatology
, to determine which acne-fighting ingredients were safe to use during pregnancy and which ingredients to avoid. Based on this, we eliminated any products that contained the following:
Retinoids/Retinol:
Dr. Viola notes that because vitamin A is essential for fetal development, "the vitamin A in retinoids/retinol can easily be transferred from mother to baby via the placenta in amounts far larger than needed, making it a no-go during pregnancy." This can potentially lead to developmental issues, so be cautious of any treatments containing this ingredient.
Parabens:
Dr. Goldfaden points out that "parabens have been shown to cause cell changes in animals and should be avoided not only during pregnancy but always."
We also excluded products with high doses of salicylic acid. According to Dr. Goldfaden, high doses of salicylic acid can act as blood thinners, which in some cases could lead to miscarriage when used continuously. Both the American Academy of Dermatology and Dr. Viola agree that using salicylic acid in small doses — around 2 percent or less — and limiting its use to small areas of the face should not cause harmful side effects.
After compiling an initial list of 20 pregnancy-safe acne treatments, we further narrowed it down based on results from the
2024 Pregnancy-Safe Beauty Awards
, where over 1,300 moms voted on their favorite skincare products, including those that treat acne. We also considered recommendations from What to Expect community members, as their endorsements suggest the products are worth considering.

Thayers' formula
features certified organic witch hazel, which can help reduce the appearance of pores, balance oily skin, and keep your skin barrier healthy. When used after a cleanser and before treatments like

Something to note: A few of the dermatologists we spoke to, including Dr. Viola, mentioned that treating acne scarring may be challenging during pregnancy. Most traditional interventions, such as retinoids, chemical peels, and procedures like microdermabrasion, aren’t pregnancy-safe and should be avoided. Dr. Viola suggests focusing on preventing and treating acne as effectively as possible during pregnancy, and then consulting your dermatologist after your baby is born to explore additional treatments if needed.

FAQ
What is the best treatment for pregnancy during acne?
Unfortunately, there isn’t a one-size-fits-all approach when it comes to pregnancy acne. You might need to try a few products before you find what’s right for you. To help solve ongoing breakouts, it’s always a good idea to establish a routine. An effective cleanser, treatment and moisturizer like the products we recommended above are a good place to start. If you find you’re still having issues with acne, consult your dermatologist.

Why I Chose Ritual Prenatal Vitamins for My Second Pregnancy
by
Melissa Bykofsky
Medically Reviewed
by
Jennifer Wu, M.D., F.A.C.O.G.
Medical Review Policy
All What to Expect content that addresses health or safety is medically reviewed by a team of vetted health professionals. Our
Medical
Review Board includes OB/GYNs, pediatricians, infectious disease specialists, doulas, lactation counselors, endocrinologists, fertility specialists and more.
We believe you should always know the source of the information you're reading. Learn more about
our editorial and medical review policies
.
| August 18, 2025
Latest update:
See more
Ritual / Ava Suwal
And right now, you can save 40% on your first month of a Ritual subscription
Just so you know, What to Expect may earn commissions from the shopping links included on this page. All sales and prices are accurate at the time of publishing.
What is it?
Ritual Prenatal Vitamins
Why I love it:
The nutrient-packed vitamins are easy to swallow and shipped right to your door, so you always have prenatals on hand.
How much is it?
$39/month
Where to buy it:
Ritual
,
Amazon
and
Target
Ritual Prenatal Sale
: Get
40% off your first month of Ritual subscriptions
— including the
Essential Prenatal Vitamin
— now through September 2.
I always assumed that, once you were ready to start trying to conceive, your OB/GYN would prescribe you a prenatal vitamin. As it turns out, doctors deem us completely capable of choosing one of the many
over-the-counter prenatal vitamins
. So when I became pregnant with my first child in 2020, I did what any indecisive journalist would do: I researched. In my internet exploration, I saw a lot of positive buzz about Ritual prenatal vitamins. And, given that I was pregnant during COVID-19, I liked that I could avoid stores and have vitamins sent to me. So I placed my order and never looked back.
Now, four years later, I’m taking Ritual prenatal vitamins again as I await the arrival of Baby #2. Suffice to say, this prenatal vitamin is well worth the hype (and higher price tag, but more on that later.)
What Are Ritual Prenatal Vitamins?
Ritual prenatal vitamins are one of the many vitamins offered by the popular supplement subscription service. In fact, Ritual was actually founded by a mom-to-be who struggled to find a prenatal vitamin she deemed to be free of “questionable ingredients.”
The brand prides itself on only using ingredients that can be traced right to the source, providing detailed descriptions about where each vitamin and mineral comes from so you know exactly what you're putting in your body. And, as an added assurance, all of the vitamins are made of GMO-free, plant-based ingredients. (Yes, vegans. You can enjoy these, too!)
Many moms-to-be praise Ritual’s prenatals for being easy to swallow and having little to no aftertaste — two things I can attest to. And, like me, Ritual subscribers appreciate the convenience of the vitamin being delivered to your door. Again, my first pregnancy was during the pandemic, so picking up anything at a pharmacy was tough. This time around, I have a toddler to manage and the delivery takes one thing off my plate.
Ritual Prenatal Vitamins at a Glance
Before I subscribed to Ritual’s Prenatal Vitamins, I talked to my friend who is a pharmacist and mom of two about the prenatals she used. Although she required prescription prenatals, she said Ritual’s prenatals were comparable to hers in amounts for all of the important vitamins. I also checked with my OB/GYN, who gave them the all clear.
Ritual’s prenatal vitamins contain choline and DHA, which aid in neural tube, brain and blood support. But not all prenatal vitamins contain them, requiring women to purchase and take separate supplements. They also contain 333% of your daily recommended value of vitamin D, which is a rarity in any multivitamin, let alone prenatals.
Ritual Prenatal Vitamins
Pregnancy supplement subscription
$39/month
See More
Available at Ritual
It's worth noting that Ritual’s prenatal vitamins don't contain zinc or vitamins A or C, though your regular diet should provide enough of each nutrient. If not, talk to your doctor to see if you should be supplementing separately.
Another important consideration: Ritual vitamins contain folate, not
folic acid
. Although both are forms of vitamin B9, folic acid is the synthetic form of folate that's proven to help prevent major birth defects of baby's brain and spine. Ritual assures it contains enough folate to be absorbed and work like folic. If you have concerns, however, talk to your doctor.

Pros
Convenient
I am the type who only realizes I am running low on something when it’s gone. Not ideal when it comes to a daily prenatal vitamin. So the fact that I can place an order once and be set for the next nine months is a true game-changer.
Of course, shipping delays can happen and you may want a backup supply on hand. Fortunately, Ritual’s prenatals are also sold at Amazon and Target. (You can actually set up a subscription through Amazon, and get a slightly reduced rate.)
I also want to take a moment to highlight Ritual’s amazing customer service. During my first pregnancy, I moved and forgot to update my address. I notified the company and they not only rerouted my order but also overnighted me an extra bottle free of charge so I wouldn't miss a pill.
Easy to Take
One of the things that drew me to Ritual’s prenatal vitamins were their size: They seemed smaller and more manageable than other prenatal vitamins, which were comparable to horse pills. Knowing I would have to take these daily. I needed something that would go down without issues. Plus, they are a softgel, which are easier to swallow than uncoated tablets.
Though I could tell the vitamins were smaller, I wasn’t sure what to expect taste-wise. Based on everything I read about prenatal vitamins, I was prepared for some chalky and fishy flavors. But Ritual’s vitamins were fine. Not the most delicious thing I’ve ever eaten, but better than what friends had warned me about. It probably helps that the vitamins are available in two flavors: citrus and mint. I opted for citrus both times (though, it was the only option during my first pregnancy) and found it to taste a lot like a vitamin C supplement. Each bottle comes with a little scent bar, so if you find the flavor too strong you can probably take that out as soon as your order arrives. This way the vitamins aren’t sitting with the flavor the entire month.
Minimal to No Side Effects
Prenatal vitamins can cause mild side effects, like constipation, nausea and vomiting. I, fortunately, haven’t had any issues with gas, nausea or fish breath. This may be in part because I take my prenatal at night before bed, which may help ease side effects. But many
What to Expect community members
had similar experiences, with one saying she, “takes them on an empty stomach and doesn’t feel bad at all.”
Considerations
One very obvious downside to Ritual vitamins is the cost. I pay a recurring $39 monthly charge by subscribing through Ritual, but you could pay almost $50 a bottle if you buy from another retailer. There are plenty of easy-to-swallow prenatal vitamins that pack just as much nutrition at a lower cost. Not to mention, you have to take two Ritual prenatals a day, whereas many other prenatals only require one a day.
Is Ritual a Good Prenatal Vitamin?
When I started my search for a prenatal vitamin, my doctor told me that unless I have any specific high risks or genetic factors — which I did not — the best prenatal vitamin was the one I would take daily. For me, that meant the vitamin had to be easy to swallow, have a tolerable taste and minimal to no side effects.
Ritual’s prenatal vitamins
checked all those boxes, and had that added convenience of being delivered to me monthly, so I would never run low.
Understandably, price may be a barrier for some moms-to-be. If that’s the case, there are plenty of comparable prenatal vitamins that cost less. But I was able to afford it, and the convenience of not having to think about ordering more before they ran out was worth the extra money. If price is not a barrier and you want a prenatal that’s easy to take and delivered to you, then Ritual’s prenatal vitamins may be it.

How What to Expect Chooses the Best Products for Parents
Shopping for baby gear can be exciting — but it’s also one of the most overwhelming parts of preparing for parenthood. In fact,
1 in 3 moms
say there are “too many baby product options” out there.¹ You’ve got enough on your plate (and in your cart). That’s where
What to Expect
comes in — not just as a trusted resource, but as your smart-shopping sidekick.
Whether you’re stumped by which
pregnancy pillow
to buy or on the hunt for a
breast pump
that actually fits your lifestyle, we bring expert insight, real-parent reviews, and medically reviewed advice — all tailored to what matters most to you.
That’s where What to Expect comes in — not just as a trusted resource, but as your smart-shopping sidekick.
We make the process easier with
product guides
that are deeply researched, medically vetted when needed, and grounded in everyday parent experience.
Why Parents Trust What to Expect
What to Expect
is the
#1 most trusted source
for product guidance among moms 18 to 44 — ranking ahead of social media, influencers, friends, and family.¹ That trust shapes everything we do.
Our content reaches
9 in 10 first-time expecting moms in the U.S.
, registering over two-thirds of pregnancies.²
Our product recommendations are rooted in real-life parent insight, informed by medical professionals, and shaped by the feedback of millions of parents and parents-to-be in our community. Editors follow rigorous research standards, and every guide is reviewed by vetted OB/GYNs, pediatricians, or other credible experts — ensuring that every pick is safe, reliable, and truly helpful for your growing family.
Behind the Scenes: How We Vet New Products
Each product undergoes multiple checks — from scanning for safety recalls, to expert board review, to real-world staff testing. Our internal litmus test? “Would I use this for my own baby?”
If the answer’s yes, only then does the product make it into our guides.
What Goes Into Our Product Recommendations
We take product research seriously because we know how much is riding on the right pick. Our editorial process includes:
What We Do
Why It Matters
In-depth research
We assess safety, design, value, and innovation across brands.
Expert insight
Our
Medical Review Board
checks health and safety accuracy.
Hands-on testing
Staff and contributors test gear in real-life parenting scenarios.
Community feedback
Thousands of parents tell us what actually works.
Product checks
We monitor pricing trends and recall alerts.
We routinely refresh content for accuracy in pricing, availability, and safety — as verified via the
Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC)
database.
Good to know:
Some of the shopping links in our product coverage may earn us a commission, but that never influences what products we choose to feature.
Each product undergoes multiple checks — from scanning for safety recalls, to expert board review, to real-world staff testing.
Our Awards: Voted by Parents, Backed by Research
Each year, we recognize products that consistently stand out — and those awards matter. Studies show
1 in 2 moms
are more likely to trust a product labeled “mom-approved” or “award-winning.”¹
Our Mom Must-Have, Feeding, Sleep, and Pregnancy-Safe Beauty programs are shaped by community voting, editor insight, and expert oversight.
Mom Must-Have Awards
This community-powered program highlights products parents love across 30 essential categories. More than 4,800 votes determined the winners, which include everything from prenatal vitamins to strollers and baby skincare.
What to Expect
Feeding Awards
We started with a list of trusted items based on community recommendations and editor testing. Then, we asked parents to weigh in. Nearly 6,000 votes across 24 categories helped us spotlight feeding essentials that consistently deliver.
What to Expect
Sleep Awards
To find the products that help families get more rest, we asked more than 800 parents to vote on their favorite sleep gear. From swaddles and sound machines to gliders and lotions, every winner was chosen based on real-world results and thousands of parent comments.
What to Expect
How We Cover Sales
Raising a child comes with costs — and smart savings matter. That’s why we only feature price drops that offer real value and reflect the lowest pricing we’ve seen in the past three months.
We don’t report on every single sale. Instead, we focus on
deals that help parents save on gear they actually need
.
How to Use Our Product Guides and Reviews
Here’s how to get the most out of our guides:
Scan Our Top Picks:
Jump straight to standout products tailored for specific needs — whether it’s “best for small spaces” or “most budget-friendly.”
Look for product accolades:
Each listing highlights its standout strength — like “best for reflux” or “most affordable.”
Read the pros and cons:
Every pick includes insights from real parents in our community, plus testing and research from our editorial team.
Spot the award badge:
Products that won our Mom Must-Have, Sleep, or Feeding Awards were voted on by thousands of parents and approved by expert reviewers.
Check for updates:
Our guides are refreshed regularly to reflect new feedback, research, and safety news.
Want to Pitch a Product?

What’s Inside the Amazon Baby Registry Welcome Box?
by
Caroline Picard
| January 16, 2025
Latest update:
See more
Caroline Picard / Adrianna Grezak
A first-time mom shares what she’d keep — and toss — from Amazon’s Baby Registry Welcome Box.
Just so you know, What to Expect may earn commissions from the shopping links included on this page. All sales and prices are accurate at the time of publishing.
Summary
The Amazon Baby Registry Welcome Box is super easy to claim and comes with a carefully curated selection of goodies from beloved baby brands like Dr. Brown’s, CeraVe Baby and MAM. It also includes several coupons and a parenting guide that first-time moms and dads are sure to find helpful.
As a first-time mom, I couldn’t wait to start my
baby registry
. Partly because it was a great distraction from morning sickness, but mostly because it made becoming a parent feel so much more real. Given how easy it is to shop on Amazon, it’s no surprise it was one of the first registries I created. And, of course, I didn’t hesitate to claim the Amazon Baby Registry
Welcome Box
.
I didn’t know much about what was inside the welcome box when I claimed it, which made opening it even more exciting. I wasn’t expecting something extravagant like a
breast pump
or a complete baby wardrobe. But with
Amazon's baby registry
being so popular — and offering an endless variety of products — I figured it had to be good.
Caroline Picard
Here’s What’s Inside the Amazon Baby Registry Welcome Box
Although the specific items may vary (and Amazon is upfront about that), all welcome boxes include a mix of baby essentials, sample-sized skincare products and several coupons for services perfect for first-time parents.
Full-size products:
Amazon Essentials Newborn Bodysuit
Amazing Baby Cotton Muslin Swaddle
MAM Easy Start Anti-Colic Bottle
and
Pacifier
Dr. Brown's Anti-Colic Bottle
A small reusable Amazon-branded bag
Caroline Picard
Sample-size products:
Lasinoh Nursing Pads
and
Breastmilk Storage Bags
Cerave Baby Moisturizing Lotion
(1 fl oz)
Liquid IV Electrolyte Drink Mix
(3 0.56-oz sticks in assorted flavors)
A high-vision contrast card
Caroline Picard
Coupons:
Shutterfly: 50% off order and 10 free birth announcements
Trust & Will: $100 off an individual or couples will
Fuel Factor: $200 off
On top of the freebies and deals, there’s also an Amazon Baby Registry guide. Think of it as a quick-reference booklet with tips for first-time parents about feeding, diapering and getting your baby to sleep. As Senior Health Editor for What to Expect, I’m constantly exposed to this kind of info, but I could see it being a handy resource for parents overwhelmed by the endless sea of advice out there.
Overall, I was impressed with the box’s thoughtfully curated selection of practical items. The MAM and Dr. Brown’s bottles were especially useful, giving me the chance to try both popular brands and discover which will be my baby’s
preferred bottle
. The sample-sized Lansinoh nursing pads and breastmilk storage bags are perfect for slipping into my purse for on-the-go convenience. As for the reusable Amazon-branded bag, I can use it to keep diapering essentials like wipes, cream, and extra onesies neatly organized when out and about.
How to Claim your Amazon Baby Registry Welcome Box
It’s relatively easy to
get your Amazon Baby Registry Welcome Box
, especially compared to other brands:
Sign up for an
Amazon Prime membership
if you don’t already have one.
Start an
Amazon baby registry
.
Add at least 10 items from Amazon’s
registry checklist
.
Ensure at least $10 worth of items is purchased and shipped from your registry. (Note: You don’t have to make the purchase yourself, but the order must ship before you can request your box.)
Click the “Claim Now” button on the “Benefits and Welcome Box” page.
Amazon Baby Registry Welcome Box vs. Other Registry Welcome Boxes
Compared to
Babylist’s welcome box
, the Amazon Baby Registry Welcome Box includes fewer items. However, all the products are from trusted baby brands that my colleagues and What to Expect Community members consistently rave about. (Plus, I wasn’t looking to be buried in clutter!)
One standout feature of Amazon’s box is that it includes something for mom. The Liquid IV hydration mixes are perfect for labor and postpartum recovery — times when staying hydrated is extra important. I haven’t seen anything like that in other boxes, and honestly, it was such a thoughtful touch!
Another pleasant surprise? Amazon under-promised and over-delivered on the shipping time. When I claimed my box, I was told it would take three to four weeks to arrive, but it showed up within just a few days. Maybe I got lucky, but that speedy delivery could be a real bonus for moms-to-be who weren’t able to claim their box earlier.
Is the Amazon Baby Registry Welcome Box Worth It?
Although it’s not as bountiful as some others, the Amazon Baby Registry Welcome Box is definitely worth snagging — even if you have to spend the $10 yourself. (Pro tip: I added a random household item to my registry and bought it to meet the minimum purchase requirement. Easy peasy!) Amazon does a great job of including a curated mix of practical essentials and nice-to-haves from popular brands.
I’m especially excited about the muslin swaddle — complete with an adorable zebra pattern! — and I’m super appreciative of the bottles and bodysuit. The one piece of advice I keep hearing? Pad the wardrobe, because blowouts happen. A lot.

The Registry Gift WTE Parents Say Helped Most After Baby Arrived
by
Elizabeth Buxton
| March 12, 2026

Door Dash
A food delivery service means one less thing to worry about when newborn life makes cooking nearly impossible.
Just so you know, What to Expect may earn commissions from the shopping links included on this page. All sales and prices are accurate at the time of publishing.
When you’re building a baby registry, most of your energy goes into the gear. The stroller you spent weeks researching. The bassinet everyone swears by. The bottles that promise less gas. Those things absolutely matter. But after baby arrives, you quickly realize the hardest part of the newborn stage isn’t choosing the right products. It’s managing everyday life while running on almost no sleep.
One thing that comes up again and again in the What to Expect community? Food. Between feedings, pediatrician visits, and long nights, something as simple as figuring out dinner can suddenly feel overwhelming. That’s why many families recommend adding some kind of meal support to your registry, whether that’s a meal train, restaurant gift cards, or a food delivery credit.
Food delivery services like
DoorDash
pop up often in community threads. Moms talk about using it to order dinner after a long day, grab lunch during a contact nap or send a quick grocery order when the fridge is empty. In those early weeks, it’s the kind of convenience that ends up making a bigger difference than you expect.
Helpful During Postpartum Recovery
For many, the ability to order food instead of cooking is especially helpful while recovering physically after birth. Inormally love cooking and make most of our meals at home, but after my C-section, even standing at the stove felt like too much. We ended up relying on
DoorDash
far more than I expected, ordering both takeout and groceries during those first few weeks when cooking just wasn’t happening.
Support During Difficult Moments
Food delivery can also be helpful during more unexpected situations. A friend of mine experienced this when her baby spent a month in the NICU. Our friend group pooled together and sent her and her husband a
DoorDash
gift card so they could easily order meals to the hotel they were staying in near the hospital. It was a small gesture, but it made a stressful and exhausting time a little easier to navigate.
Why Many Add It to Their Registry
Friends and family naturally gravitate toward buying baby gear, but once the baby arrives, what often helps most is support with everyday life. Adding something like a
DoorDash
gift card to your registry gives people an easy way to help when the newborn haze hits. And unlike most baby items, it doesn’t take up any space in your house.
Door Dash Gift Card
Mom-Favorite Registry Gift
$10
See More
See More
It Comes in Handy During Pregnancy, Too
Food delivery doesn’t just come up after baby arrives. It’s also a common theme in pregnancy threads, especially during the first trimester when nausea and food aversions can make cooking feel impossible, something I experienced myself when even thinking about making dinner felt like too much.
In one recent
What to Expect community discussion
, a mom at nine weeks pregnant wrote that she and her husband had been ordering DoorDash almost every day because “everything in our fridge makes me want to gag.” Others quickly chimed in saying the same thing: leftovers suddenly looked disgusting, cravings changed daily and sometimes the only thing that sounded edible was something specific they could quickly order. (If you have a pregnant friend who is currently going through it, consider sending a little DoorDash credit. It might end up being exactly what she needs.)
Other Food Support Parents Appreciate
Some families mix in restaurant-specific gift cards depending on what’s available locally, and many organize meal trains, or coordinate takeout drop-offs with friends. But across the What to Expect community, the takeaway is the same: in those early newborn weeks, and sometimes even earlier in pregnancy, having an easy way to get a meal on the table can be surprisingly helpful.
After covering baby gear for years and building my own registries, I’ve learned that the most useful gifts aren’t always the big-ticket ones. Sometimes they’re the small things that make day-to-day life easier while you adjust to life with a newborn.

I Got the Babylist Welcome Box — Here’s What’s Inside the $8.95 Box Everyone Talks About
by
Leah Rocketto
| January 1, 2026
Latest update:
See more
Leah Rocketto / Adrianna Grezak
Curious about the Babylist Welcome Box (a.k.a. Hello Baby Box)? Here’s what was inside my 2026 box — from full-size gear to sample essentials.
Just so you know, What to Expect may earn commissions from the shopping links included on this page. All sales and prices are accurate at the time of publishing.
Babylist Welcome Box Quick Review
The Babylist Welcome Box is filled with a sweet mix of baby gear — and the contents change regularly, so it’s always a bit of a surprise.
As of August 2025, you’ll find sample-sized goodies from Huggies, Honest Company, and Tubby Todd.
Feeding time is covered, too, with gear from Dr. Brown’s, Momcozy, and Lansinoh.
There’s also baby clothing from Kyte and Primary, plus coupons to help you save on more must-haves.
The small shipping fee of $8.95 is worth it for a box valued at $100 — and possibly more once you count the coupons.
When I was pregnant with my first baby, I rushed into creating a
baby registry
without knowing all the best-kept
registry hacks
. Now, as a soon-to-be mom of two, I’m older, wiser, and far more strategic — which is why signing up for a
Babylist registry
(and snagging their famous
Welcome Box
) was at the top of my to-do list.
Over the years, friends have raved about the variety of trusted brands tucked inside — think Huggies, Tubby Todd, Dr. Brown’s, and more.
Caroline Picard
, What to Expect’s deputy editor and new mom, puts it best:
“Calling the Babylist Welcome Box ‘generous’ feels like an understatement,” says Caroline. “One of the highlights for me was the selection of diapers, wipes, and butt cream samples. While they’re not big-ticket items, the cost of experimenting with different brands adds up."
And she’s right — for just $8.95 in shipping, you get over $100 worth of baby gear. That’s money saved and decision-making made easier (and yes, maybe even a little sanity preserved).
Having a chance to test several without committing to full-size purchases felt like a real win.
Caroline Picard, What to Expect Deputy Editor and mom of one
What’s Inside the Babylist Welcome Box 2026
The 2026 Babylist Welcome Box proves that good things really do come in small packages. My spring box included baby clothing, feeding gear, postpartum treats, and a surprising number of coupons for free or discounted goodies.
The 2026 Babylist Welcome Box is well-stocked with samples from beloved brands.
Leah Rocketto
According to Babylist (and the many What to Expect Community threads I’ve scrolled through), the box’s contents change about twice a year. So what your sister-in-law got last fall might not be what you find inside yours this spring — but the variety and quality stay consistent.
Here’s what was inside my spring 2026 Babylist Welcome Box:
Full-size Products:
One of my favorite items in the 2026 Babylist Welcome Box: Soft bodysuits from Kyte Baby and Primary.
Leah Rocketto
Primary “Hello Sunshine” bodysuit (3-6 months)
Kyte Baby bodysuit (0-3 months)
Dr. Brown’s Natural Flow Anti-Colic Options+ Narrow Baby Bottle (4 oz.)
Philips Avent Natural Baby Bottle (4 oz.)
Suavinex Pacifier (0-6 months)
Bibs Pacifier (0-6 months)
Beaufort Bonnet Company burp cloth
Stonyfield Organic bib
Sample-size Products:
Babylist stocks their welcome box with diapering samples — perfect for traveling or testing before investing in full-size products.
Leah Rocketto
WaterWipes (10-count)
Honest Clean Conscious Wipes (10-count)
Ubbi Baby Wipes (25-count)
Healthy Baby Diapers, Size 1 (2-count)
Huggies Skin Essentials Diapers, Size 1 (3-count)
Triple Paste Diaper Cream (two 0.21 oz. packs)
Tubby Todd All Over Ointment (0.17 oz.)
Noodle & Boo Newborn 2-in-1 Hair and Body Wash (0.5 oz.)
Noodle & Boo Newborn Super Soft Lotion (0.5 oz.)
Palmer's Cocoa Butter Formula Skin Therapy Oil (0.68 oz.)
Momcozy Breastmilk Storage Bags (7-count)
Lansinoh Breastmilk Storage Bags (3-count)
Lansinoh Nursing Pads (2-count)
Lansinoh Nipple Balm (0.05 oz.)
Coupons and Freebies:
20% off Primary coupon
20% off Kyte Baby sleep bag
Free Colored Organics bodysuit
Free Little Unicorn swaddle
Free Bobbie formula (one can)
Free Tinybeans+ subscription (one month)
Free TinyBeans photo book
10 free Shutterfly birth announcements
It’s a low-cost way to try trusted brands without fully committing to products that may not work for your baby.
How to Get the Babylist Welcome Box
Start a
Babylist registry
.
Add at least 40% of items from the Babylist registry checklist.
Add three items from other stores.
Make a $30 purchase from the Babylist Shop (or wait for a gift-giver to do it).
Verify your address and pay $8.95 for shipping.
Even though I already had a lot from my first pregnancy, meeting the criteria was easier than expected. Exclusive Babylist bundles like the Bottle Box and Pacifier Box made it simple to fill in gaps.
Caroline, on the other hand, used Babylist as her primary registry and said meeting the criteria was a breeze.
How Does Babylist Compare to Other Registry Welcome Boxes?
Compared to the Amazon Welcome Box, the Babylist Welcome Box comes out ahead in both quantity and brand quality. Caroline especially appreciated the inclusion of products for moms — something other boxes sometimes skip.
Yes, the $8.95 shipping fee is a minor downside, especially since some registry welcome boxes are free. But with a retail value of $100, it’s an easy decision for me.
Is the Babylist Welcome Box Worth It?
Between the generous mix of full-size products, the
variety of sample-size items
, and the stack of coupons for even more freebies, the Babylist Welcome Box is worth far more than the small shipping fee.
In short: The Babylist Welcome Box contains $100-worth of baby items that you'll be happy to have on hand.
Leah Rocketto
It’s a low-cost way to try trusted brands without fully committing — and as any parent knows, what works for one baby might not work for the next. Even though I know which products Olivia liked, Baby #2 could have entirely different preferences. Consider this box your test-drive for baby gear, with plenty of perks along the way.
In short: Add the Babylist Welcome Box to your registry checklist — your budget (and your curiosity) will thank you.
Babylist Welcome Box FAQ
Can international users receive the box?
Unfortunately, the Babylist Welcome Box is only available to U.S. residents At this time, it can’t be shipped internationally or to APO (Army Post Office), FPO (Fleet Post Office), or DPO (Diplomatic Post Office) addresses.
What brands are typically included in the Babylist Welcome Box?
Much like the products themselves, the brands featured in the Babylist Welcome Box change regularly. Based on my own experience — and plenty of conversations with other moms-to-be — some of the most popular brands included in the Babylist Welcome Box include:
Aquaphor
Beaufort Bonnet Company
Desitin
Dr. Brown’s
Healthy Baby
Honest Company
Huggies
Kyte Baby
Lansinoh
Lovevery
Momcozy
monica + andy
Motif
Nanobébé
Palmer's
Pampers
Philips Avent
Primary
Triple Paste
Tubby Todd
WaterWipes
Are the products in the Babylist Welcome Box sized for newborns only?
The clothing in the Babylist Welcome Box is usually sized for newborns or 0 to 3 months. Non-clothing items can often be used well into your baby’s first six months — and in some cases, even longer.
Can someone trigger the $30 Babylist Welcome Box purchase on my behalf?
Yes! If someone buys a gift of $30 or more from your Babylist registry, it counts toward the purchase requirement for the Babylist Welcome Box. But if you’re as excited (and impatient) as I was, you can always make the purchase yourself and get your box on the way sooner.

There are so many
baby registries
that you might be tempted to skip one altogether. I almost did — and that would have been a huge mistake.
A registry isn’t just a wishlist for loved ones (though it does help prevent those well-meaning but not-quite-your-style gifts). It’s also a personal
baby gear checklist
, a way to
score discounts
, and, in some cases, your ticket to a box full of
free baby samples
.
So… what’s the best baby registry? Well, that depends on your needs. Luckily, I’ve done the legwork — between two pregnancies, years of testing, and reviewing gear for What to Expect, plus plenty of conversations with other parents — to break down the pros, cons, and perks of each.
Pro tip:
You don’t have to commit to just one registry. In fact, doubling up can mean double the perks!
How I Tested and Chose the Best Baby Registries
To find the best baby registries for different kinds of parents, I:
Tested multiple registries myself during each of my two pregnancies, tracking ease of use, product selection, and perks.
Spoke with three What to Expect staffers who’ve built registries during their own pregnancies to learn what worked — and what they’d change.
Scoured the What to Expect Community boards for registry reviews, focusing on their feedback about building and ordering from each one.
Whether you choose just one or decide to go with a few, you can’t go wrong with these choices. And if you're still unsure which registries to sign up for
What to Expect's Baby Registry Builder
for personalized suggestions based on your preferences.
Why Trust Us?
What to Expect is the world’s most trusted pregnancy and parenting brand for a reason. Our product recommendations are based on expert parent insight, advice from medical professionals and feedback from the millions of parents and parents-to-be in our community. Our editors adhere to the highest research and reporting standards and our team of vetted OB/GYNs, pediatricians and other health professionals ensure our recommended products are safe and effective for you and your baby.

Amazon Baby Registry
Available at
Amazon

Why We Love It
Based on the advice of hundreds of What to Expect parents, I chose
Amazon Baby Registry
as my primary registry. In addition to the wide selection of products, I appreciated that I could add anything to my registry, even if it’s not strictly baby-related.
Since I received a lot of hand-me-downs, I included some household essentials on my registry — things like paper towels, laundry detergent, and even
high-protein snacks
to keep me fueled while breastfeeding. This was a huge sanity-saver during those early newborn days when my brain was scattered, and neither my husband nor I could leave the house.
Sarah Darby
, What to Expect's Senior SEO Content Strategist, created an Amazon registry during her second pregnancy to take advantage of the amazing perks, rather than to share with friends and family.
"I loved the welcome kit, the vast array of options, the completion discount, and the ease of getting everything shipped right to me," she says.
But if you do share your registry with others, Amazon’s Baby Registry is super easy to use. It’s likely your loved ones already have an account, making it easy for them to buy gifts from your list while shopping for themselves. The simpler you make it for them, the more likely you are to get everything you asked for (fingers crossed!).
Used by
Leah Rocketto
,
soon-to-be mom of two and What to Expect's Associate Shopping Director:
“With Amazon's wide selection of products, it was easy to find exactly what I wanted, like a car seat and stroller.”
Amazon baby registry features and perks:
Return policy:
Return gifts within one year of shipping notification.
Discount:
Amazon’s 15% completion discount
starts 60 days before your due date and ends 90 days after (up to two orders, totaling $2,000 max).
Freebies:
Prime members get a
free welcome box
with samples and coupons after adding 10 checklist items and receiving a $10 purchase from the registry.
Group gifting:
Yes
Universal registry:
No

Anything that wasn’t purchased on Babylist, I added to my Amazon registry to use the completion discount. Why We Love It
I love how easy it is to use
Target’s baby registry
, especially when pregnancy brain kicks in. You have to join Target Circle first (don’t worry — it’s free) before you can create a registry. Once you do, an "Add to Registry" button appears on every product to ease registry inclusion. There’s also a cute calendar icon with your due date and a spot for a custom message that everyone sees when they visit your registry. I personally appreciated that I could let people know which products were most important by labeling them "most wanted."
Another big selling point: the sheer number of Target locations across the country — about 1,900 stores — means I could check out products in person before committing, rather than relying solely on online reviews. Sarah used Target's registry during her first pregnancy and also appreciated the in-person option.
One potential downside to the Target baby registry is that their selection of strollers and car seats is more limited compared to Amazon. For instance, my stroller of choice, the UppaBaby Vista V2, wasn’t available at Target. So, if I had chosen to stick with only one registry, I would have had to pick a different option or buy it myself.
Another thing to note: Target offers two 15% discounts, which are automatically added to your Target Circle account and applied to your next purchase. If you don’t want to use it right away, be sure to deselect “Offer Saved” in your Target Circle Offers page to temporarily deactivate the coupon. That said, having a Target registry gives you access to exclusive deals on baby items — up to 20% off! — for up to a year after your due date. This was huge when I was running low on diapers and wipes, and Sarah found it helpful postpartum.
"As a first-time mom, I didn't really know what I needed until I needed it, so being able to save even after my completion discount ended was helpful," she says.
Used by
Sarah Darby
, mom of two and What to Expect Senior SEO Strategist:
"I noticed that my 'more wise' family members did shop in store, while most people shopped online but it was nice to have both options. I actually went to the store to buy most of what I didn't get at my shower, which was a really fun and exciting experience as a first-time mom."

Want to save your friends and family money on their gifts for baby? A

And if Walmart doesn’t have the best price? Simply bring proof that one of their online competitors offers a lower price on the exact same, in-stock product, and Walmart will price match. (This applies to one item per day.)
Don’t sleep on Walmart for baby clothes either. Since my daughter was born, Walmart has been my go-to for cute, high-quality clothing. Seriously, their Garanimals line is on par with Cat & Jack! Plus, the retailer partners with brands like Carter's, Monica + Andy, Gerber and others to create exclusive, affordable lines.

Why We Love It
Parents-to-be love
Babylist
because, in addition to purchasing products directly from Babylist, it gives you (and gift-givers) the option to buy from other retailers. It also allows you to add anything to your registry from any store on the web.
“When I was pregnant with Lou, I had no idea where to start with a registry and felt totally overwhelmed,”
says
Liz Buxton
,
What to Expect's Shopping Director and mom of one
.
“I went with Babylist because I could corral everything I actually wanted — from everyday Amazon basics to random Etsy finds — in one easy-to-share spot.”
Beyond products, you can even register for cash funds (college, diapers) or request help from friends and family.
“I liked that Babylist had the option to add non-monetary things like ‘walking the dog’ or ‘home-cooked meal,’” says Jeanne Beacom, What to Expect’s Sr. Campaign Manager, speaking to Babylist’s versatility. “I added links to sewing patterns if people wanted to sew something for baby and maternal health charities to my registry.”
Babylist also offers plenty of sample registries to help you get started, keeping in mind that no two parents will need the exact same things. They provide examples for second-time moms, parents expecting multiples, adoptive parents of older babies, and single moms, explaining why each product fits these parents' specific needs.
The only downside to Babylist is that some gift-givers can get frustrated with the checkout process. If someone buys a gift from a store other than Babylist, they have to leave the site and then return to mark the gift as purchased. That said, it’s your baby registry, and Babylist's logistical challenges are minor in the grand scheme.
Used by

“With Babylist, I liked being able to compare prices, link other registries, and add things to my list during a middle-of-the-night scroll.”

But the ultimate perk parents are loving: Costco is a partner with

One great feature is the link that allows you to see the popular items people are adding to their registries, so you can stay in-the-know when it comes to the latest and greatest. Baby Registry FAQs
Should I set up more than one baby registry?
I recommend signing up for more than one baby registry. Not only will you score extra discounts (hello, more savings on baby gear!), but you can also opt in to multiple welcome boxes — meaning more free baby samples for you and your little one.
It can be a lot to keep track of, which is why I suggest using
What to Expect's Baby Registry Builder
. It keeps all your registries in one place, so you can spend less time juggling lists and more time dreaming about those newborn snuggles.
What’s the best universal registry?
The best universal registry is Babylist, which allows you to add items from Amazon, Target, and directly from brands.
Can I add services like housecleaning or cash funds to my registry?
Babylist and MyRegistry allow you to add services or cash funds.
When should I create my registry and how early?
Most parents-to-be start their baby registry somewhere between 12 and 20 weeks of pregnancy. That sweet spot gives you plenty of time to browse, compare, and daydream about all the tiny things you’ll soon be using — without feeling rushed. Plus, your list will be ready to go before those baby shower invites head out, so loved ones have plenty of time to shop for your little one’s soon-to-be favorite things.

What I’m Adding to My Baby Registry the Second Time Around
by
Leah Rocketto
| April 2, 2026
Latest update:
See more
Stocksy
Here’s what I regret skipping the first time and what I won’t bother with for Baby #2.
Just so you know, What to Expect may earn commissions from the shopping links included on this page. All sales and prices are accurate at the time of publishing.
Hi all! I’m Leah, a What to Expect editor, casual-turned-professional deal hunter and mom to a 3-year-old named Olivia. I also have another baby girl on the way. Now that I’m well into my second trimester, my second baby registry is officially underway.
This time, I’m bringing both my editorial experience (over a decade researching and writing about baby gear) and the real-life lessons that come from surviving the newborn phase.
I’ve been thinking about the sanity-saving items I bought in a panic (portable night lights were a surprise win), the so-called must-haves that collected dust (I was overly ambitious about mastering a wrap carrier) and the tried-and-true gear I used nonstop and plan to use again.
Here’s what I’ll be registering for before Baby #2 arrives — and what I’ve learned to skip.
Baby Gear Worth the Investment
Mockingbird Single-to-Double Stroller
: Sleek, easy to maneuver and just as versatile as higher-end strollers (but at a fraction of the price).
Chicco Fit360 Rotating Car Seat
: This car seat works from day one through the booster stage. The rotating base was especially helpful while recovering from delivery.
mamaRoo Multi-Motion Baby Swing
: This swing kept Olivia calm and soothed. It even earned the nickname “mamaPoo” in our house thanks to its magical effect on baby digestion.
Fisher-Price 3-in-1 Sensory Gym
: A true tummy-time MVP. The six repositionable toys kept Olivia engaged through a tough milestone.
Ergobaby Mesh Baby Carrier
: Comfortable, lightweight and easy to use even in those sleep-deprived early days.
Nursery Essentials
The Ollie Swaddle
: The only swaddle I could manage while half-asleep under dim nightlight. Simple and secure.
Nanit Pro Baby Monitor + Floor Stand
: Clear video and helpful sleep insights gave us peace of mind and helped us build a loose nap schedule.
Hatch Rest Sound Machine
: Customizable sound and light settings that even my mom could figure out.
Feeding Must-Haves
Nuk Simply Natural Baby Bottles
: Designed to support combo feeding, with multiple holes for a natural flow and a wide neck for easier latch.
The First Years Modular Steam Sterilizer
: After many late nights boiling bottles on the stove, my mom gifted me this compact, time-saving model.
Konny Baby Bibs
: Cute enough to be worn as an outfit accessory, but super absorbent too.
Comfy Cubs Muslin Burp Cloths
: Soft, durable and affordable. I kept a stash in every room.
Boppy Nursing Pillow
: This helped with positioning during breastfeeding and doubled as a tummy time support pillow.
ChookaChoo Teething Mittens
: Most teethers don’t stay in your baby’s hands, but these actually do.
Changing Table MVPs
WaterWipes
: A clean formula that’s gentle on sensitive skin and easy to toss in the diaper bag.
Tubby Todd All-Over Ointment
: Great for diaper rash, eczema and dry skin. A little goes a long way.
Bumco Baby Bum Brush
: This silicone spatula kept my hands mess-free, especially when we were on the go.
Oogiebear Nose and Ear Cleaner
: The soft silicone loop made it easy to remove dried boogies and ear wax without a fight.
haakaa Baby Nail File
: Less nerve-wracking than clippers. The built-in light made trimming feel more precise.
Bath Time Basics
Aveeno Baby Body Wash and Lotion
: Gentle and effective, especially for Olivia’s sensitive skin. I’ve been an Aveeno fan for years.
KeaBabies Hooded Towels
: Some of the thickest and softest towels I’ve found. They made post-bath drying quick and cozy.
Frida Baby Grow-With-Me Tub
: Smart design that grows with your baby and doesn’t take over the bathroom.
Small (but Mighty) Sanity Savers
Miss Mouth’s Messy Eater Stain Treater
: This miracle spray tackled every stain, from blowouts to spaghetti nights. I use it on my clothes too.
Skip Hop Elbow Saver and Kneeler
: Made long baths on cold tile much more bearable.
Anico EASZZZ Baby Night Light
: Compact and portable with a soft glow that’s ideal for late-night feeds and changes.
Yogasleep Hushh Portable Sound Machine
: Clips onto the stroller or crib and blocks out noise anywhere we go.
What I’m Skipping This Time
Button-Up Pajamas
: They’re cute, but impractical. Zippers and magnets are much easier in the middle of the night.
Wipe Warmers
: Not worth the space, and your baby won’t mind room-temperature wipes for long.
Bottle Warmers
: We used a mug of warm water instead. Worked just fine.
Wrap Carriers
: Tried one. Got tangled. Gave up.
Too Many Toys
: Babies mostly sleep, eat, and poop. A few toys for tummy time and car rides are plenty.
Final Thoughts
Even with years of product research under my belt, I still got a few things wrong the first time. But those lessons made curating this second registry easier, smarter, and more realistic.
I hope my experience helps make your registry process a little smoother too. In the end, trust your instincts — you're a mom, after all. You know what your growing family needs most.

We tried out the Target baby registry to see how it fares against the rest — the results are in.
Back to Top
In This Article
The benefits of a Target registry
How to create a Target registry
Using your Target baby registry
Our review
The perfect baby registry seamlessly combines a wide selection of products with perks like discounts, cool features and a forgiving return policy. It should come with completion discounts (a discount you get near your due date), free shipping on orders with low totals (around $30) and ways to make the registering process as smooth as possible. Target hits all those marks.
Read on to find out why Target has one of the
best baby registries
. (And if you're interested in personalized recommendations for where to register and what to add to your registry,
check out What to Expect's Baby Registry Builder
.)
Just so you know, What to Expect may earn commissions from the shopping links included on this page.
The benefits of a Target baby registry
Completion bonus:
Eight weeks before your arrival date, Target emails you a 15% off coupon that you can use twice. Your registry even has a countdown with the number of days until you get your discount. It's important to note that one of those discounts is added to your Target Circle account and automatically applied to your next purchase. If you do not want to use it on your next purchase, be sure to deselect “Offer Saved” in your
Target Circle Offers
page to temporarily deactivate the coupon. Also important: the coupon expires after six months, so make sure to use it before you lose it.
Bonus deals:
The savings don't stop once the baby is born. Throughout the first year, Target sends 20% off coupons to use on best-sellers tied to various milestones.
Year-long return policy:
Target’s standard return policy gives you only 90 days to return a purchase, but they allow you to return gift registry items for up to a year after your due date. Something to keep in mind: All your gifts need to be new, unopened and in the original packaging to be considered for a return. That means if you take the tags off and wash all of your onesies before you deliver, but baby never fits into the newborn size, you won't be able to return them.
Checklist:
Target provides a checklist to make sure you add everything you need (because it can be hard to keep track). The products are divided into different categories, and each one has a tracker that lets you know how much of the checklist you’ve completed so far.
Welcome Kit:
Once you create your registry, you’re eligible to get a Welcome Kit. Valued at $100, the mix of coupons and
free samples
will be sent to your home after you add 10 items to your registry
and
make a purchase of $10 or more.
Shopping assistance:
Overwhelmed by all the baby gear? Target's Baby Concierge service can help. Launched in 2026, this free service pairs you with a baby specialist who, after a phone call, provides product recommendations that best fit your lifestyle, needs, and budget.
Must-haves and special notes:
Target lets you mark which items on your registry you deem as "most wanted," which is a simple way to make shopping easier for loved ones and increase the chances you get all your essentials. (Target says items marked as must-haves are twice as likely to be bought!) You can also add special notes to items that loved ones can see, like "My mom used to read me this book all the time, and I want to do the same with my little one!" or "This swaddle set is so adorable, especially in the color yellow."
How to create a Target baby registry
Before you can create a Target Baby Registry, you have to sign up for Target Cricle (don't worry — it's free!) Once that's complete, navigate to
Target’s Baby Registry page
and click “create registry.” Then the fun part begins. You get to put in your due date, choose a unique URL for your registry — think something like “baby-girl-smith” — and add your gift address. There's also a place to share the sex of your baby and a customized note to loved ones checking out your registry (if you want to!).
How to use the registry checklist
Creating a registry can be overwhelming — especially for first-time parents. Target’s checklist helps them figure out what they actually need to get through the first year (Real answer? Sleep! Unfortunately, that's
not
on the site). If you're already overwhelmed by options, you'll appreciate that Target does some of that work for you.
The checklist consists of 12 categories — like diapering, feeding and nursery furniture — that each have smaller subcategories within them. For example, the nursery furniture category lists a bassinet, a crib, a crib mattress, a changing table and a glider or rocker. Target doesn’t seem to overdo the lists and includes what parents actually need.
Once you add the suggested items to your list (or decide you don’t need them), you can check a box next to the category name. As you add items to your list and check off boxes, Target will keep track of how many areas you’ve completed on your checklist. The feeding section may say “5/13 complete,” while the clothing section says “7/7 complete.” There’s no pressure to complete everything, but the checklist helps you spot what you’re missing.
How to use the registry gift tracker
Next to the checklist, you’ll find your gift tracker. This area has some spoilers, because you can see what was purchased and who bought it. Luckily, you have to click a button that says "show me the names" when you try to track a gift to see who bought it for you, so that you don't totally ruin the surprise by accident. Thanks, Target! Otherwise, you can browse the list of gifts and even check off a box next to each one after you send a thank-you note.
Using your Target baby registry
Can we tell you how much we love this registry? Once we signed up, it was easy to find where everything was thanks to helpful buttons and an intuituve layout, which meant we didn't have to do a lot of digging. We jumped right to adding items and registered for a car seat, some cute bath toys, and a pack of pacifiers. We didn't feel limited by the selection and found everything we needed. We also loved playing around with the checklist and were obsessed with the countdown to the baby's arrival, so long as you decide to put it in (it's like waiting for the ball to drop on New Year's Eve!). We also appreciated Target's helpful explanations of what different gear is for. For instance, if you go to select a travel system, the site easily and clearly explains the difference between a modular and full-size system. Overall, the entire experience was impressive and painless.
How to return a registry gift
If you get two high chairs, it’s easy to return the second one.
In your registry, go to the "offers & benefits" section on the home page and select "start a return." From there, you'll select what item you want to return and the store you want to take it back to. You'll then get a special barcode that Guest Services will scan in the store, so bring that and your unopened gift when you make your Target run. You’ll get your refund as a Target gift card.
Pros
The app keeps you organized and makes returns easier
A full year to make returns
A helpful checklist to keep you on track
The completion discount, Circle Bonuses, and Welcome Kit help you save money during baby's first year
Cons
Gifts need to be returned in person
Our review
The Target baby registry gives you plenty of things to love. From the easy-to-use checklist to the year-long return policy, Target is doing almost everything right with this registry. Plus, there are over 1,900 Target stores in 50 states, so chances are good that you and your friends and family have one close by.
We can’t believe we’re saying this: In many ways, Target has a better baby registry than Amazon. Yes, we're dethroning the ruler of all baby registries. Why? Most importantly, Target’s registry is so easy to use, especially with the app. You can use the scanner on your phone to organize and adjust all of your registry items. And on the website, all the buttons you need are at the top: My Registry, Add Items, Checklist, Gift Tracker and more. Plus, if you ever navigate away from your registry to another part of the site, there’s a very visible “Registry” button at the top of all the site's pages that will take you back to your registry’s main page. We’ve tested many different baby registries, and Target’s ease of use tops the list.
Then there’s the design. We were actually happy to log onto our registry page. There's a bunch of helpful modules organized clearly and thoughtful on the home page so you can find everything you're looking for, and sweet details like a countdown to your arrival date and how many gifts are left on the list. We have a profile photo at the top left and a space for a fun message to any gift givers that come to the page. The whole experience is calming, and it makes you look forward to filling out the registry list.
Some of the features go above and beyond what we’ve seen with other baby registries. This registry has a “Most Wanted” box next to each item on your registry, so you can let friends and family know what to prioritize. The group gifting option takes the pressure off people who don’t want to overspend, but it still allows you to get everything you need off the list. The checklist is easy to use and doesn’t add unnecessary pressure when you’re already dealing with so much (Amazon’s checklist, for instance, is a bit overwhelming). The completion discount is among the highest we’ve seen, and you can combine it with your 5 percent discount if you have a RedCard or Target Circle offers.
Target also has a great selection of products both online and in stores, and the amount of locations around the country means you can pop into your local store at any time to see what a product looks like in person.
