Why the Windi the Gaspasser Has Become a Must-Have Baby Accessory for Me
by
Brigitt Earley
| January 1, 2026
Latest update:
See more
This clever tool helped my twins with their digestive issues, and they even slept better after using it.
What to Expect selects products based on independent research and suggestions from our community of millions of parents; learn more about our
review process
. We may earn commissions from shopping links.
What is it?
Fridababy Windi the Gaspasser
Why I love it:
It gave my twins relief from their digestive discomfort and even helped them sleep better.
How much is it?
$13
Where to buy it:
Amazon
I thought I had seen and done it all when the
NoseFrida Snotsucker
entered my life. Little did I know, I’d hit an all new low (or high?) three kids later.
My boy-girl twins have always needed a little help in the number two department. I’ve never met a baby with more trapped gas than my son, and my daughter typically doesn’t poop more than once a week. But both of their issues have left us with the same problem: they’re constantly squirming and fussing as they try to work through their respective digestive issues.
During one of our earlier pediatrician visits, the doctor offhandedly suggested we try
Fridababy’s Windi the Gaspasser
($13 on Amazon).
What is the Fridababy Windi exactly? Well, I think the packaging explains it quite well: “It’s maybe a little strange. It’s a doctor-invented hollow tube that safely, naturally, and instantly relieves gas and calms colic — no ingestible remedies or drops necessary.”
Here’s how it works:
Massage baby’s belly gently downward.
(I typically use my forearm and roll it downward.)
Lubricate the tip of the Windi.
(I use the suggested product: coconut oil.)
Lift baby’s legs and insert the Windi
like a rectal thermometer and wait for the telltale whistle — a.k.a. baby passing gas.
Strange, indeed. But, as I’ve come to discover, it’s also very effective.
With four kids under the age of 4, I’m no stranger to a rectal thermometer, and that definitely helped my comfort level the first time I used the Windi. My nerves were also quelled by the fact that the shape of the Windi doesn’t allow you to go too far — it has a stopper that flares out to prevent you from doing just that.
So I forged ahead, starting with my gassy son. I gently massaged his belly, then proceeded to insert the tube. The Windi went in easily, thanks to the lubrication — it didn’t seem like he felt a single thing. And almost instantly, I heard a decent mass of air pass through the Windi. I wouldn’t call it a whistle like the kind a teapot might make, but there was no questioning what was happening when I heard the gentle blow.
I repeated the process a few times, with toots coming out each time. (Note: Though the packaging warns you might expel much more than a few farts — have a diaper handy, they say! — I didn’t get anything more than air.) It seemed like my son’s entire body instantly relaxed.
Wow
, I thought, as I moved on to my daughter.
The Windi is disposable (and certainly shouldn’t be shared between children), so I tossed the first one, washed my hands and grabbed a fresh one.
Though I used the same amount of lubricant, it didn’t glide in quite as easily, but it also didn’t seem like it was uncomfortable in any way. (Chalk it up to a difference in bodies, I guess.) But this time, I got much more than air. I got an entire diaper’s worth of the sludgiest breast milk poop I have ever seen — at full force. Thank goodness, I took the advice and kept the diaper under her bum throughout the process! For what it’s worth, I also recommend placing baby on a muslin cloth or
changing pad
for extra protection. It really can get messy — I’ve even had drops of poop shoot up onto my own shirt.
It’s worth noting that it took much longer for the Windi to work it’s magic on my daughter. (And the same thing has happened with my son every so often.) The company says it should only take a few seconds, but I found that sometimes you have to be patient and sit there for a minute, stop and massage the tummy for a good couple of minutes, or ever-so-gently push down on the rectum a bit with the Windi.
One thing is for sure, though: Once the Windi does what it's supposed to, you can instantly see the relief in baby’s eyes and feel it in your little one’s belly. I’ve also noticed my kids sleep so much better when we use the Windi, since they aren’t trying to work through gas or aren’t all backed up.
The company says you can use the product up to six times a day (my own pediatrician suggested no more than three times per day to let their muscles develop on their own). From about 8 to 16 weeks, I used the product on each of them at least once per day. But now, at 5 months, their abs are strong enough to begin doing their own work. As a result, we’ve dialed it back to just once or twice a week when it seems like someone is struggling.
It’s truly a miracle worker, and one I’ll undoubtedly be gifting to any new mom I know — even if they look at me like,
What in the world did you just give me
. It may be strange, but trust me, it’s so worth having this little helper in your back pocket.

How to Clean Baby Clothes
by
Maria Masters
| March 3, 2022
Latest update:
See more
Everything you need to do (and buy) to safely clean baby's essentials.
You already knew that having a baby meant round-the-clock feedings and diaper changes — but round-the-clock loads of laundry? Welcome to parenthood!
In fact, if you’re like many of the parents in our
What to Expect community
, you may be doing nearly one load of laundry a day — everything from soiled diapers, to spit-up soaked onsies, to baby food-stained shirts and bibs.
The good news: Cleaning baby clothing isn’t necessarily difficult (just time-consuming). “
Baby clothes
tend to be made out of material that is very easily washable, like 100 percent cotton,” says
Jessica Ek
, a spokesperson for the American Cleaning Institute. Follow these steps.
What to Expect selects products based on independent research and suggestions from our community of millions of parents; learn more about our
review process
. We may earn commissions from shopping links.
What you'll need
Ready for your umpteenth load of laundry? Here’s what you’ll need.
Award-winning detergent
Dreft Stage 1: Newborn Hypoallergenic Liquid Baby Laundry Detergent
$16
See More
Laundry detergent:
While you
don’t need to buy a baby-specific brand
, it’s a good idea to opt for
fragrance-free detergents
, since fragrances can irritate some babies’ sensitive skin.
Dreft Liquid Baby Detergent
($16 for a two-pack on
Amazon
) is a good hypoallergenic option, and a perennial favorite among What to Expect community members.
Drying rack (optional):
Baby clothes are often made of cotton, which is especially prone to shrinking. To prevent your 3-month onesies from dwindling to a newborn size, consider lying the baby clothes to dry on a rack like
this one
. (Short on time and prefer the dryer? See below.)
Laundry mesh bag:
The laundry tool you never knew you needed,
a garment bag
keeps tiny socks, hats and mittens from going missing in the dryer.
Dish soap:
Many
parents in the What to Expect community
rave about dish soap (particularly this classic option from
Dawn
) for any and all stains — baby poop included.
How often should you wash baby clothes?
It’s a good idea to wash anything with poop or spit-up on it right away. “You want to make sure you clean up bodily fluids regularly because they might grow germs on them,” says Ek. “Especially because
[newborns] don’t have fully developed immune systems
yet.”
Track your baby's diapers with the What to Expect app
Babies aren’t outside playing in the mud all day, but they can still make quite a mess. Here are step-by-step instructions for cleaning baby clothing.
Step 1: Check for residue
If there’s a build-up of residue (spit-up, breastmilk, formula, poop) on the clothing, wipe it up with a paper towel. This can absorb the excess gunk.
Maria Masters
Step 2: Set your rinse cycle to a cool water temperature
Cool water should take out most of the stains on your baby’s clothes, many of which are made of 100 percent cotton, but it won’t shrink the fabric like a hotter temperature will.
But there are a few exceptions, says Ek: You may need to use a hot rinse setting — which is harsher than cool rinse, but more effective at removing stains — on waxy stains like greasy baby oil or chocolate. In this case, the hot water can help “melt” stains.
Step 3: Toss the baby clothing into the machine with other dirty laundry
Maria Masters
Unless your child requires a different detergent (like
Seventh Generation's Free & Clear Laundry Detergent
for extra-sensitive skin), you don’t need to wash baby clothes separately from those of the rest of the family. Just be sure to separate the colors from the whites; while most modern clothing is made with pretty color-fast dyes, it’s possible that the colors can bleed together, staining your white clothing.
Step 4: Add about 2 tablespoons of detergent (or use the measuring cup on the lid)
Maria Masters
It’s important not to use too much detergent. If you go overboard, the wash cycle might not rinse all the detergent off, leaving a sticky residue that could be irritating to your baby’s skin.
Step 5: Check for stains before drying clothes
After the load is done, check the clothing to see if the stain came out in the wash. Between the mix of the water, laundry detergent and agitation from the washer (all that churning and tumbling the machine does), most stains will have come out, says Ek. If not, throw it back for another wash — do
not
put it in the dryer. The heat from the dryer can “set” the stain, making it harder to come out.
Step 6: Hang the clothes up to dry
It’s a good idea to hang dry clothing — especially 100 percent cotton clothing, which is prone to shrinking — instead of putting it in the dryer. If you prefer to use the dryer, switch it to a lower temperature setting and try to take out the clothing right after its done.
One time when it’s actually
good
to throw your baby clothes in the dryer, says Ek: When there’s a stomach bug going around the house. The high heat can help get rid of the germs.
How to clean poop from baby clothes
If a diaper blow-out happens, follow the steps above. If you’re on-the-go or won’t be able to wash the clothing for quite a few hours, try running the stain under cold water or putting some dish soap (or even hand soap) on it in the meantime. This might help the stain come off easier once you can put it in the washing machine. Or if you're in a pinch, having a stain stick is another great option, says Ek. Parents in the What to Expect community and beyond rave about the
Babyganics Stain Eraser Marker
($9 for a three-pack on
Amazon
).
How to clean baby cloth diapers
Because
cloth diapers
can get very soiled, you’ll want to wash them separately from your other clothes, ideally every day or other day, says Ek. Scrape off the solid waste and, if you’re not throwing it in the wash right away, soak the diapers in cold water. Then, toss the cloth diapers in the washing machine and set the temperature to cool or cold water (check the care instructions on the diaper to be sure).
After the load is done, you may want to rinse the diapers again in cold water to make sure all the detergent is gone (again, a good reason not to use too much detergent). Don’t use fabric softeners, though — these products can make the diapers less absorbent (and you definitely don’t want
that
). Then, set them on a rack to dry. Putting baby clothes in the dryer subjects the fabrics to high temperatures, causing them to break down faster.
One note: Most cloth diaper companies provide pretty comprehensive cleaning instructions, so it’s important to follow them whenever you can, says Ek.
How to clean heirloom baby clothes
If the clothes are highly valuable or particularly sentimental, consider taking them to a professional laundry service, says Ek. If you want to DIY, try hand-washing the garment first to see how it goes.
First, apply a little detergent on an inconspicuous spot on the clothing to make sure it doesn’t damage the fabric. (You might also try a detergent that’s formulated for delicate clothes, like
Woolite
.) Then, hand-wash the garment in cold or warm water — not hot. “The threads are going to be more delicate,” says Ek.
Next, lay the garment out on a drying rack to dry. You might also consider patting the clothing — particularly any areas that have lace or embroidery on them — with a clean towel, in case any of the color dye runs, she says.

Cleveland Clinic,

, August 2021.

, Senior Director, Digital Communications at the American Cleaning Institute, Washington, DC.

How to Clean Baby Toys
by
Maria Masters
| April 15, 2022
Latest update:
See more
From wooden blocks to stuffed animals, here’s what you should know about cleaning baby’s toys, and how to do it.
Baby toys can end up in some pretty icky places — on the floor, under the couch, in the toilet. More concerning, though, is where those toys go next (yep, you guessed it: baby’s mouth).
While there’s no need to start sanitizing everything in sight — most household bugs aren’t harmful, anyway — you might want to keep some supplies on hand to wipe down your child’s favorite toys.
Cleaning your baby’s toys, however, can be trickier than
cleaning your baby’s clothing
or bedding, in part because many of them weren’t made for endless cycles in the dishwasher or washing machine, says Jessica Ek, a spokesperson for the American Cleaning Institute.
For a step-by-step guide to cleaning your tot’s toys, follow these steps.
What to Expect selects products based on independent research and suggestions from our community of millions of parents; learn more about our
review process
. We may earn commissions from shopping links.
What you'll need
Use these supplies to clean baby’s toys at home or on the go.
Award-winning detergent
Dreft Stage 1: Newborn Hypoallergenic Liquid Baby Laundry Detergent
$20
See More
Laundry detergent:
You don’t need to spring for a baby-specific brand, but if your child has sensitive skin, you may want to choose a mild, hypoallergenic option like
Dreft Liquid Baby Detergent
($20 for a two-pack on
Amazon
).
Laundry mesh bag:
Washing a beloved stuffed animal? A
mesh bag
can help keep tiny buttons or plastic eyes from going missing in the washing machine and dryer.
Dish soap:
Many wooden or plastic toys can be cleaned with mild dish soap.
This one from Babyganics
is a favorite among parents in the What to Expect community.
Disinfecting wipes:
Disinfecting wipes kill off bacteria and viruses. Parents in the WTE community like
these ones from Seventh Generation
.
Handy disinfecting wipes
Seventh-Generation Disinfecting Multi-Surface Wipes
$6
See More
Fragrance-free soap
Babyganics Foaming Dish & Bottle Soap
$21
See More
How often should you clean baby toys?
If a toy is visibly dirty — for example, you can see dirt or food on it — you should wash it off, says Ek. Likewise, if someone in your home is sick, it’s a good idea to
disinfect the objects that that they’ve touched
at least once a day to help prevent the spread of germs.
There’s no need to break out the big gloves, though. Most germs around the home aren’t particularly harmful, and
exposing your baby to some germs
can even help shore up his immune system and fend off infections later on.
How to clean wooden baby toys
Wooden toys
are among the most straightforward objects to clean, says Ek. Here’s how to do it.
Step 1: Wet a washcloth with dish soap
Dab some mild dish soap onto a washcloth and wipe off the toys.
Step 2: Let the toys air dry
The toy will still be damp, so you’ll want to let them dry off before giving them back to your child.
How to clean plastic baby toys
Plastic toys can also be easy to clean, though if they have electronic components to them, you’ll want to take care not to get those ones wet, says Ek. Here are a few steps.
Step 1: Wet a washcloth with dish soap
Use a mild dish soap to remove the dirt from the surface of the plastic toy, being careful not to get any water on any electronic parts. Toys that are made of entirely plastic (including pacifiers) as well as ones designed for the bath can also likely go in the top rack of the dishwasher, says Ek.
Maria Masters
Step 2: Let the toys air dry
Let the toys dry off before giving them back to your baby.
How to disinfect toys
To kill bacteria and viruses that may be lingering on the surface of your toys, you can use a disinfectant wipe, says Ek. Make sure to let the disinfectant liquid dry completely, and then rinse it off and let it dry again.
You want to make sure the toy is completely dry and residue-free before giving it back to your baby, especially if your little one can put it in their mouth, she says.
How to clean baby stuffed toys
Many stuffed animals and other plush toys are machine washable (though you can check the tag for specific instructions). Here’s how to clean your baby’s beloved teddy.
Step 1: Put the toy in a garment bag
Stuffed animals can have plastic eyes, noses and buttons that can go missing in the wash, so your best bet is to put them in a garment bag before placing them in the washing machine. If you don’t have a garment bag, you can always use a pillowcase.
Step 2: Wash on delicate in cold water
Washing the toys on a gentle cycle — and in cold water — reduces the wear and tear on the toys. Unlike baby clothing, plush toys aren’t meant for multiple rounds in the washing machine. Hot water can also be harsher on materials than a cold rinse. “These toys are often well-loved, and you don’t want to damage them,” says Ek.
Maria Masters
Step 3: Toss the toy in the dryer on low or dry it with a hairdryer
Leave the toy in the garment bag or pillowcase and place it in the dryer (with or without other laundry) on a low setting, says Ek. Or, simply dry the toy with a hair dryer. While it’s possible to air-dry the stuffed toy, that can be trickier to do when the weather is warm. “If it’s a really humid day in the summer, air-drying might not dry it fast enough, and there may be an opportunity for mold to grow on it,” she says.

Even before I started
trying to conceive
my first baby, I was fascinated by the idea of understanding my menstrual cycle. But while predicting when my period would arrive felt relatively straightforward,
pinpointing ovulation
was a whole different ballgame. At the time, I was shocked by how many methods and technologies promised to help. Fast forward to today, and there are even more options on the market.
Overwhelmed? I know the feeling. Over the last five years, I’ve tried 10 different fertility trackers (when I wasn’t pregnant with my two babies), ranging from sophisticated wearables and smart thermometers to classic test strips. Each provided me with useful data and insights to keep tabs on my cycle and better understand my
fertile window
. Together, they helped me plan two pregnancies and even troubleshoot a few fertility issues along the way.
How I Tested the Best Fertility Trackers
Over the past five years, I put 10 different fertility trackers to the test — not just for a week or two, but across multiple menstrual cycles to see how they performed through both predictable ovulation patterns and the surprise curveballs our bodies like to throw. Here’s the specifics on how I evaluated each option:
Consistency across multiple cycles:
I followed each tracker’s instructions closely, logging data every day  to see how well it detected patterns over a five-year period. Experts note that an accurate picture of your fertility requires regular, daily use.
Predicted vs. actual ovulation:
I tracked basal body temperature (BBT), cervical mucus, and LH surge results to measure accuracy.
Ease of use:
This will depend largely on your lifestyle and preferences, but I noted how intuitive each fertility tracker was to set up, how much effort it required for effective results, and whether it fit naturally into my morning or bedtime routines.
Long-term cost:
I noted upfront prices as well as ongoing costs (like replacement strips or subscription fees) to understand the real investment (and if it was worth the splurge).
Expert advice and guidance:
I also consulted with Dr.
Brian A Levine
, M.D., attending physician at Lenox Hill Hospital in New York City, and
Dr. Tarun Jain
, M.D., MSc, medical director of Northwestern Fertility and Reproductive Medicine and professor of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Northwestern University, to gain a greater understanding of how fertility monitors work and which features matter most depending on your cycle.
After all that testing (and lots of
BBT charting
), I narrowed my initial findings down to just eight trackers I’d personally vouch for and recommend. These are the products that stood out to me for their accuracy, usability, and versatility.
But because no two pregnancy journeys are the same and everyone’s body is different, I also tapped into the What to Expect Community and our editors on staff to gather additional feedback from fellow moms who’ve put these devices (and others!) through the wringer, too. In doing so, I increased the final list to the 10 best fertility trackers, below.
A Doctor's Note on Fertility Trackers
“Fertility awareness is important, and apps and tools are a positive thing,” says Dr. Levine. “But remember: They’re just guides. The best assessment is seeing a fertility doctor and having an
ultrasound
and blood work.”
According to Dr. Jain, beginners should start with BBT thermometers or ovulation predictor kits to first understand their cycles. For those in need of more detailed data, he shares, “Wearables can be a good investment, especially if you prefer not to manually track symptoms.” Both, he adds, can benefit those with irregular cycle patterns.
However, there are a number of factors that can influence accuracy. “Consistency is key for accurate readings, especially with BBT and wearable devices. Track at the same time each day and in similar conditions,” Dr. Jain explains. “Health factors like stress, illness, medication, sleep patterns, and lifestyle habits can impact readings.”

Types of Fertility Monitors
Some women can track their fertile window by simply analyzing changes in
their
cervical mucus
or charting their basal body temperature. But many benefit from analyzing other forms of biometric data via a fertility tracker, notes
Dr. Jain
. The
emerging market of sophisticated fertility monitors can make it rather difficult to decide whether you want a wearable, app, or hormone monitor.
Below, I've outlined the main types of fertility trackers based on expert insights:
Hormone Monitors:
These fertility monitors calculate hormone levels on a digital device and aim to identify your fertile window and ovulation date. These devices typically collect a urine sample, which calculates hormone levels like estrogen, luteinizing hormone (LH), and progesterone. Some hormone monitors link with an app to chart your data.
Thermometers:
During the menstrual cycle, your body’s temperature at rest — or basal body temperature (BBT) — rises after ovulation. By tracking your temperature, you can confirm that ovulation has occurred and get a sense of when your ovulation typically occurs each month if your cycles are fairly regular. Some thermometers link with an app to help you track your cycle. However, Dr. Jain
warns that accuracy can easily be thwarted by illness, sleep disturbances, alcohol, or inconsistent measurement times.
Wearables:
Wearable fertility monitors are designed to catch your body’s lowest temperature, typically overnight, and are worn on your wrist, arm or fingers. Some fertility monitors collect additional data, like heart rate and sleep patterns. Another type of wearable fertility monitor goes in the vagina and assesses changes in cervical mucus texture and consistency that indicate fertility.
Test Strips:
A low-tech but trusted way to track your own fertility is with ovulation test strips or progesterone test strips. These test for LH, which peaks 24 to 48 hours before ovulation occurs, or progesterone, which rises after ovulation to indicate ovulation has occurred. You have to read and track changes in the strips yourself, but there are apps to help! There’s no smart functionality here (you simply urinate on them), but it’s a relatively affordable and a basic, yet effective option.
Saliva Monitors:
Saliva can change in consistency during fertile windows due to estrogen. These are typically reusable and non-invasive, but can be tricky to interpret correctly, Dr. Jain points out.

Fertility Trackers FAQs
What are fertility trackers?
Fertility trackers are devices that help you to identify your fertile window and ovulation date. If you are trying to conceive, fertility trackers can help you identify the best days to try to get pregnant. Fertility trackers can also help you understand your cycle and fertility.
How accurate are fertility trackers?
It is hard to assess the accuracy of fertility trackers as a whole, as they all function differently, but most devices have been proven to increase your chances of getting pregnant. Depending on your specific body, certain fertility trackers may be better than others for accurately predicting ovulation.
“The most fertile period is the five days leading up to ovulation and the day of ovulation itself,” Dr. Jain says.
How do fertility trackers work?
Fertility trackers work in three main ways: tracking hormone level changes, tracking body temperature changes and tracking cervical mucus changes. Fertility trackers that detect hormone levels typically track the rise of estrogen and/or LH, which indicates ovulation is coming. Temperature trackers look for a rise of BBT above baseline, which occurs after ovulation as progesterone rises. Cervical trackers look for changes in cervical fluid that occur during the fertile window.
How long do I need to track before expecting results and when should I consider seeing a fertility specialist?
For those under the age of 35, Dr. Jain recommends seeing a specialist after 12 months of trying. Those who are older should consider seeing a specialist after 6 months, but adds, “Immediate evaluation is recommended if there are known fertility issues (e.g., irregular periods, endometriosis, history of pelvic infections).”

Shopping for a baby is, in a word, overwhelming. The sheer number of parenting and
pregnancy products
on the market (and
how much it'll cost
to get all that gear) alone is enough to send any new mom or dad into a shopping spiral. But when you find a product that truly makes life easier, whether that buys you five extra minutes of sleep or helps soothe your little one faster, it’s a win worth celebrating.
That’s exactly what the What to Expect Mom Must-Have Awards are all about. This year’s winners are the products parents actually use, love, and recommend.
You know there are some non-negotiables, like a
car seat
and
stroller
, but others, while not crucial to your child’s survival, can feel just as essential as a new parent. Things like a
baby carrier
that gives your arms a break when your whole body is tired, or even a TikTok-viral product that actually lives up to the hype. (Heads up: Both are on the list below!)
How the Mom Must-Have Winners Were Chosen
No two babies (or parents) are the same. What works like magic for one family might flop for another. But when thousands of What to Expect parents agree on a singular favorite, you know it’s something special.
Our Mom Must-Have winners are chosen by the millions-strong What to Expect community, meaning every pick has been mom-tested and -approved. This year, more than 8,000 votes poured in across 20 categories, from maternity must-haves to baby gear and beyond. The products that rose to the top are the ones parents truly rely on day after day (and, yes, night after sleepless night). This way, new parents everywhere can shop with confidence (and maybe skip a few of those “oops, didn’t need that” purchases, too).
Without further ado, here are the winners of the
2025 What to Expect Mom Must-Have Awards
.
Kathleen Felton orginally contributed to this article.
Why Trust Us?
What to Expect is the world’s most trusted pregnancy and parenting brand for a reason. Our product recommendations are based on expert parent insight, advice from medical professionals and feedback from the millions of parents and parents-to-be in our community. Our editors adhere to the highest research and reporting standards and our team of vetted OB/GYNs, pediatricians and other health professionals ensure our recommended products are safe and effective for you and your baby.

Momcozy’s pillow, which was also a 2023 winner, has a U shape that hugs and gently supports your entire body, including your head, back, neck and feet. The pillow is so plush and the material so soft and cozy, that many moms say they continue to use it postpartum to provide support for nursing, sleeping or just sitting.

As with all convertible car seats, the 4Ever DLX 4-in-1 adapts to your growing baby’s needs. But this particular car seat takes it the furthest, giving parents up to 10 years of use with its final stage: a backless belt positioning booster that’s suited for children between 40 and 120 pounds. Talk about stretching your dollar!
It’s also easy to install, thanks to the brand’s In Right Latch system, which allows you to quickly click it into place. However, some parents note that the harness can be difficult to tighten and the straps can be tricky to loosen, which isn’t ideal if you’re in a hurry. To start, the Vista V3’s shock-absorbing wheels make for a smooth ride, while the rain shield, bug shield and UPF 50 canopy keep your little one safe from all the elements. There’s also the massive basket beneath the seat that can hold up to 30 pounds of baby gear. Meanwhile, compatible accessories like the carry-all parent organizer and changing backpack provide more space to store your essentials. The Vista also folds and stands on its own for easy storage.
But it’s the stroller’s longevity that really wins over parents. Though it’s undeniably expensive, you can tap this stroller from the newborn stage up to 50 pounds. As your family grows, it's capable of accommodating up to three children. How many strollers do you know that can do that?

Whether you’re constantly waking up for late-night feeds, silently begging your newborn to fall back asleep or struggling through a toddler sleep regression, quality Zzzs are probably on your wishlist. And while there are countless products out there that promise to help you and your little one get more shut-eye, not everything lives up to the hype. Luckily, our community of moms have “been there, done that.” And they recently cast their votes in the sixth annual What to Expect Sleep Awards to tell you which are actually worth your hard-earned dollar.
How We Chose What to Expect’s Sleep Award Winners
Throughout the month of April, more than 800 parents cast their votes for their baby bedtime heroes across 18 different categories; everything from swaddles and sound machines to lotions and gliders. The result? An A-list of the best sleep-related baby products on the market.
Winners selected based on which nominee received the most votes. We also combed through thousands of write-in comments to learn exactly why parents love the following products.
Why Trust Us?
What to Expect is the world’s most trusted pregnancy and parenting brand for a reason. Our product recommendations are based on expert parent insight, advice from medical professionals and feedback from the millions of parents and parents-to-be in our community. Our editors adhere to the highest research and reporting standards and our team of vetted OB/GYNs, pediatricians and other health professionals ensure our recommended products are safe and effective for you and your baby.

Many caregivers swaddle their baby at night in hopes of preventing flailing arms from interrupting precious sleep. But swaddling can be tricky — especially when you're exhausted — which is why many parents turn to specially designed
swaddle blankets
with time-saving features like zippers or snaps.
According to the What to Expect community, the best of the bunch is the
SwaddleMe Original Swaddle
— an affordable, user-friendly option that’s also a back-to-back winner in the What to Expect Sleep Awards.
Using it is simple, open the swaddle’s “wings,” place your baby on top with their legs inside the bottom pouch, wrap one wing snugly around your baby, followed by the other, and fasten using the large Velcro tabs. You can adjust the wings for a secure, custom fit — ideal for even the wiggliest sleepers. The bottom zipper makes those late-night diaper changes much easier.
Another bonus: the roomy leg pocket gives your baby plenty of space to kick, which parents love. Many also note how well the swaddle holds up, even after frequent washes — a huge plus given the inevitability of overnight blowouts and spit-up.
Just remember: stop using any swaddle as soon as your baby begins to roll over.

Unlike a traditional swaddle, however, Halo’s SleepSack doesn’t hold down your baby’s arms. This is a crucial feature once your LO is able to roll over, making swaddling no longer safe.
Also known as a
wearable blanket

is a nursery must-have — and why it’s a repeat Sleep Awards winner. This nifty night light projects a wide array of colors, which you can customize using either the buttons on the machine or the intuitive app through your phone. Did we mention it plays a variety of different melodies and white noise, so it doubles as your sound machine?
What to Expect parents love the many relaxing color options and the calming, pre-programmed sounds like white noise, rain, lullabies or even the dryer to help lull baby to sleep. You can also set a timer for how long the light should stay on, in case you worry about it waking your baby up.
When your child is a little older, there are even more light functions to take advantage of, such as preprogrammed "time-to-rise," "nap time" and "bed time" settings, which you can turn on by touching one button or launching them from your phone. Birth Chart Calculator
What were the stars whispering the moment your baby arrived earthside? Just enter her birth details for a peek into your sweet pea’s planetary story.
How Does a Birth Chart Calculator Work?
Your baby’s birth chart, decoded
What you’ll see
A few helpful notes before you begin
Curious what the stars were whispering the moment your sweet pea arrived earthside? Our free birth chart tool lets you peek into the planetary story written just for your little love. Just pop in her birth details and we’ll reveal her cosmic baby book written in the sky. It’s stargazing, tailored to your tiny dreamer.
Your baby’s birth chart, decoded
Think of it like a cosmic baby book: a one-of-a-kind map of where the Sun, Moon, and planets were when your little one took her first breath. Each detail — from her rising sign to where Venus was hanging out — offers sweet insight into your baby’s personality, emotions, and growing style.
What you’ll see
Your child’s chart will look like a big starry wheel, divided into 12 “houses” (kind of like celestial rooms). Each house hosts a zodiac sign — maybe Leo in the first, Pisces in the twelfth — and the planets take their places throughout, forming a beautiful sky story.
For example: If the Moon was shining through the sign of Taurus in the second house at the time of birth, that gives your little one a Taurus Moon in the 2nd house, which could hint at a love for cozy routines, sweet treats, and lots of snuggles.
Astrologers look at all these pieces — signs, houses, planets, and their little cosmic conversations (called “aspects”) — to paint a fuller picture of your baby’s emotional rhythm, natural gifts, and soulful sparkle.
A few helpful notes before you begin
You don’t need to share your child’s full name unless you want to. Providing a nickname or initial (or even leaving it blank) is just fine. The chart is all about your baby's birth details.
For the location field, just pop in the city where your little one was born. (Typing “Boston” should give you dropdown options — go with the one that fits best.)
The exact time of birth gives the clearest chart. If you don’t know it, choose “I don’t know” — the chart will still be meaningful, just without a rising sign or house placements.
Fun fact: The Moon changes signs about every 2.5 days, so if your lovebug was born on a cusp (when one sign’s ending and another’s beginning), that timing can shift things a bit. If you’re not sure, we’ll help guide you through it.
Whether you’re a seasoned astrology lover or just feeling starry-eyed, your child’s birth chart is a tender, timeless way to explore what makes your baby so uniquely her. It’s less about prediction and more about connection.
Go ahead — take a peek at the sky the moment your tiny miracle arrived. The universe had a front-row seat.
This birth chart was created just for you with help from AI. Remember, it's just for fun.
FAQs About Birth Chart Calculator
How to read your baby’s birth chart
Astrological birth charts can be tricky to read, but our birth chart provides a full description of your baby’s astrological traits, even if you don’t have much experience with astrology or birth charts. Just plug in your baby’s data points and let our tool do the hard work!
Can I use the birth chart calculator before my baby is born?
Yes, you can test out the birth chart calculator with your due date and anticipated location and time of birth. But until your baby is born, you won’t be able to know their unique chart. That’s something to look forward after you meet your little one!
How accurate is an astrological birth chart?
Your baby could have a lot of the personality traits described in their birth chart…or not! Astrological birth charts are a lot of fun, but your baby will be a unique person with a personality all their own.

Here's how to breastfeed when your nipples are flat or inverted — and baby has trouble getting a grip.
Back to Top
In This Article
What are inverted nipples?
What are flat nipples?
Can you breastfeed with flat or inverted nipples?
What can I do about flat or inverted nipples to make breastfeeding easier?
How to treat flat or inverted nipples that become sore
You probably didn't pay too much attention to your nipples pre-pregnancy, but now that you're breastfeeding (or are pregnant and planning to breastfeed), you might give them a closer look.
Why? Because the way your nipples are shaped can impact breastfeeding. Having flat or inverted nipples might make it harder for your baby to get a firm grasp, and an improper latch can affect
how much milk
your baby gets and potentially decrease milk production.
While that may sound concerning, you shouldn’t panic. With the right care and attention, even those with flat or inverted nipples can breastfeed just fine. Here's what you need to consider.
What are inverted nipples?
Some nipples protrude out when you gently press on or squeeze the areola — the ring of pigmented skin surrounding the nipple. But when you pinch or squeeze the skin around an inverted nipple, it retracts inward instead.
Some nipples may not look inverted when you don’t try to compress them, while others might be slightly dimpled. It's possible to have inverted nipples all of your life and not know it until you begin breastfeeding. But in other cases, engorgement or swelling from IV fluids given during labor can cause temporary inversion.
If you're not sure what you’re dealing with, do the pinch test to check. Your nipple is inverted if it becomes concave instead of sticking out. Another way to spot an inverted nipple is if it doesn’t become erect when stimulated, like during sex or when exposed to cold.
If it seems like one or both of your nipples are inverted, you should let your OB/GYN or your baby's pediatrician know. An inverted nipple shape can make it tougher for babies to latch on, and in some cases, potentially affect milk flow.
Track every feed and pump in the What to Expect app
What are flat nipples?
Flat nipples neither protrude or retract inwards. Instead, they fall somewhere in the middle — giving them a flat shape that lays even with the rest of the areola.
Like with inverted nipples, it's not always easy to spot flat nipples just by looking at them. If you gently pinch or squeeze the areola and your nipple doesn't protrude but also doesn’t collapse inward, the nipple is considered flat.
And also like with inverted nipples, flat nipples can sometimes be a temporary issue caused by engorgement or swelling from IV fluids. Whether you notice nipple flatness before giving birth or it seems to develop afterwards, you should let your doctor know.
Can you breastfeed with flat or inverted nipples?
The good news is that your nipples' outward appearance has no effect on your breasts' ability to produce milk. The bad news is that a flat or inverted shape might make it harder for your baby to get a good latch and remove the milk efficiently. That can potentially result in him not getting as much milk as he needs, which can in turn negatively affect your supply.
In short, flat or inverted nipples can make breastfeeding a little tougher, especially in the beginning. But the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and lactation consultants agree that in most cases, a less-than-ideal nipple shape doesn't have to stop you from breastfeeding.
Keep in mind, too, that not all women with atypical nipple shapes run into
breastfeeding issues
. In general, babies tend to have an easier time sucking from flat nipples than inverted ones. And a baby with a strong suck might be able to draw out a mildly inverted nipple all on her own. Premature babies or those with weaker sucks might have a harder time, especially with moderate to severely inverted nipples.
What can I do about flat or inverted nipples to make breastfeeding easier?
There are lots of techniques that you can use to help "draw out" your nipples or make them longer so your baby can latch easier. Start by talking with your baby’s pediatrician or a lactation consultant, who can help you navigate options like:
Get a deep latch and try different positions
Help your baby take in more of your nipple and breast by encouraging him to open his mouth wide and over the nipple. At the same time, try to gently push back on your breast tissue to encourage your nipple to stick out.
Once he's
latched on
, his nose should be touching your breast and his lips should be flared out, sort of like a fish. Experimenting with different positions, like a
football clutch or cross-cradle hold
, can often make latching easier.
Stimulate them
You may be able to coax your nipple out with some gentle stimulation. Try either touching your nipple manually or putting it against something cold.
Breastfeed often
Going too long in between nursing sessions can cause engorgement, which may make your nipples flatten or invert. Newborns should nurse on demand — typically every two to three hours, which should add up to eight to 12 nursing sessions over a 24-hour period.
Give reverse pressure softening a go
Gently massaging the areola with your fingers for a few minutes before nursing can help ease engorgement and make your nipple protrude more, making it easier for your little one to latch.
Do a pre-feed pump
Pumping for a few seconds before nursing can help lengthen your nipples.
Don't try to go long enough to actually get milk out unless your breasts are very engorged, and the engorgement is what's causing your nipples to flatten or invert. In that case, you could experiment with pumping to ease the engorgement just enough so your nipple protrudes and your baby can latch on.
Try a tool
Breast shells — hard plastic shells worn in your bra between feedings — could potentially draw out your nipples in the early days after giving birth. Used under the guidance of a lactation counselor or doctor,
nipple shields
can also help you achieve a better latch when breastfeeding.
Manual suction devices like LatchAssist are another option that you can use for a few minutes right before nursing.
Be proactive
If you know before giving birth that your nipples are flat or inverted, it's always a good idea to talk with your OB/GYN or your baby's pediatrician. While you don't have to take steps to address your nipple shape during pregnancy, you can take steps to prepare for any possible latching issues by finding a lactation consultant who you can reach out to once the baby arrives.
How to treat flat or inverted nipples that become sore
It’s normal to experience some soreness in the early weeks of breastfeeding, especially if you have flat or inverted nipples. Your baby may be putting extra pressure on the area as he tries to draw the nipples out, which could possibly damage the skin.
Sometimes the soreness will ease up on its own in a week or two as your baby gets the hang of nursing. But if that’s not the case, meet with a lactation consultant, who can help you adjust your positioning so your baby gets a better latch (and make nursing much more comfortable).
Take care, too, to keep sore nipples clean and dry in between feedings. If you have cracked or broken skin, trapped moisture could up the risk for infection. Soaking your nipples in saline solution three to five times a day can help reduce soreness and infection risk, too.
Flat or inverted nipples can sometimes set your breastfeeding journey on a bumpy start. But with a little bit of patience and help, you can absolutely make it work — and before long, get into a comfortable nursing groove.
